result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) under demo/color-picker/App.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m]) — matches the explicit spawn declaration; no undeclared/inherited seat defect.
result.strongestDefect: L-1 — There is no entry module. `find demo -name "main.ts"` returns nothing; the application entry is the eight-line inline `<script type="module">` at demo/color-picker/index.html:205-213. Because an HTML file cannot express a composition root, App.vue IS the composition root by default, and it therefore carries five unwritten boot assumptions: (a) `app.use(router)` ran before mount (App.vue:274 → useViewManager.ts:36-41 hard-requires it; nothing declares it); (b) the pre-module fouc-guard already stamped the scheme + four `--saved-bg-n` props (index.html:159-201), agreement maintained by a hand-mirrored predicate that ground.ts:40-46 records having drifted once already; (c) the mount container is `<body>` (measured: `document.querySelector('#app') === document.body` → true); (d) App.vue is the CSS document root (four sheet imports at :199-210, one of which is the whole barrel); (e) two app-level installs — `useGlobalDark()` :214 and `provideApiClient()` :219 — run in a component setup, with correctness resting on App's setup preceding Dock's, a contract written only in the comment at :212-213. MT-F012's blank production deploy is the visible symptom of this missing file; the four structural assumptions are the invisible ones. A twelve-line `main.ts` makes (a), (d), (e) disappear, makes (c) expressible, and reduces (b) to its irreducible pre-module core.
result.negativeProof: N/A for the overall verdict (DEFECTIVE), but two axes the premise named are provably SOUND and are recorded in the report so a later wave does not re-litigate them. N-1 — the demo consumes the PUBLISHED library correctly: `grep -rn "@mkbabb/value.js" demo/ | wc -l` → 39, all through published subpaths (/color /css /easing /math /quantize, all present in package.json#exports); `grep -rn '\.\./\.\./src\|"@src' demo/ --include='*.ts' --include='*.vue'` → no output. The self-alias set is GENERATED from the exports map with anchored per-subpath regexes (vite.config.ts:39-50), so a demo import absent from `exports` fails to resolve rather than silently working — the demo structurally cannot write an import a real consumer could not. The one surviving `@src` alias is scoped by vite.config.ts:70-74 to `assets/docs/*.md` source-snippet embedding. App.vue itself imports the library not at all, which is correct for a shell. N-2 — the named three-parallel-`useDark` suspect is CURED: all nine dark consumers in demo/ use `useGlobalDark` from `@mkbabb/glass-ui/dark` (App.vue:190, useContrastSafeColor.ts:9, HeroBlob.vue:39, ConsoleRail.vue:92, useMarkdownColors.ts:1, ProfileSection.vue:8, MobileMenuDropdown.vue:6); zero vueuse `useDark`, zero local stores. N-3 — the visual audit finds nothing this component owns: 60 captures, `blankOrNearBlank 0`, `pageErrors 0`, `horizontalOverflow 0`, `darkClassMissing 0`, `mainCountNotOne 0` — App.vue's `<main>` (:47) and `<nav>` (:24) landmarks are correct on every route in every matrix, confirmed live (`mainCount: 1, navCount: 1`).

defects.defect: No entry module exists; App.vue is the composition root by default and silently carries the whole boot contract (router-plugin dependency, fouc-guard lockstep, body mount, CSS document root, two app-level installs in a component setup).
defects.evidence: `find demo -name "main.ts" -o -name "main.js"` → (no output). Entry = demo/color-picker/index.html:205-213 (inline `<script type="module">`). Assumption (a): App.vue:274 `useViewManager()` → demo/shell/useViewManager.ts:36-37 `useRouter()`/`useRoute()` then :41 `router.isReady()`. (b): index.html:159-201 fouc-guard; ground.ts:40-46 "LOCKSTEP CLAUSE 2" records the predicate having drifted (dropped 'auto' arm). (d): App.vue:199-210 four CSS imports; demo/styles/foundation.css:1,2,56,57,76,81,85 is itself the barrel. (e): App.vue:214 `useGlobalDark()`, :219 `provideApiClient()`, rationale at :212-213 = a mount-order contract in a comment. Build-side proof already measured in MT-F012.1: 698-byte application-free entry chunk, content hash `Dezn_h7o` byte-identical to a stock-Vite inline-entry repro.
defects.mechanism: missing composition root — boot logic migrates into the root component because HTML cannot express one
defects.reproduction: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/probes/vite-entry-repro/ for the build half. Structural half: remove `app.use(router)` from index.html:211 → TypeError at useViewManager.ts:41, a dependency App.vue never declares.
defects.proposedCure: Create demo/color-picker/main.ts holding createApp + `app.use(router)` + `app.provide(API_CLIENT_KEY, createApiClient())` + `initGlobalDark()` + `import "../styles/foundation.css"`, referenced as `<script type="module" src="./main.ts">`. Assumptions (a), (d), (e) become explicit compiler-checked lines; (c) becomes expressible; (b) reduces to the irreducible pre-module guard. App.vue drops both installs and all four CSS imports and becomes pure layout. Also fixes MT-F012 as a side effect — this is the form Vite documents.

defects.defect: `<body>` is simultaneously the Vue mount container and the teleport/portal host — two roles collapsed onto one element, so the app root and every portal escape hatch are siblings with no intervening app container.
defects.evidence: demo/color-picker/index.html:214 → `<body class="relative" id="app" data-paper-field></body>`. Live probe at http://localhost:9000/#/ returned `{"appIsBody": true, "appTagName": "BODY", "appLayoutParent": "BODY#app", "bodyChildCount": 5, "bodyChildren": ["DIV","DIV.app-layout","SPAN","DIV","DIV"]}` — `.app-layout` is one of five body children; the other four are teleported overlay hosts. `app.mount()` clears `container.innerHTML`, so the mount also owns body's initial children.
defects.mechanism: role collapse on one DOM node — mount container conflated with portal host
defects.reproduction: Playwright evaluate on the live dev server: `document.querySelector('#app') === document.body` → true.
defects.proposedCure:
Keep `data-paper-field` on `` (it correctly must dominate the body-portaled dialogs — index.html:203-213 documents this) and give Vue its own container: `
`, with `#app { position: relative; min-height: 100dvh }` in demo/styles/shell.css (the sheet that already owns `.app-layout` at :19). Only expressible once L-1's main.ts exists, because today the mount call lives inside the HTML that declares the body.

defects.defect: `vite.config.ts` imports an application feature composable four levels deep; `ground.ts` carries two disjoint lifetimes (browser runtime contract + node build-time HTML transform) in one module, so a build-only function ships to the browser and the build depends on app internals.
defects.evidence: vite.config.ts:15 → `import { injectGroundTokens } from "./demo/color-picker/composables/boot/ground";`. ground.ts (146 lines) splits as: runtime = GROUND_STORE_KEY/GROUND_RECORD_VERSION/GROUND_STOP_COUNT/FIRST_VISIT_GROUND/normalizeGroundStops/buildGroundRecord (consumer boot/useAtmosphere.ts); build-only = injectGroundTokens :131-146 (sole consumer vite.config.ts:150-155). Live resource probe on /#/ lists `composables/boot/ground.ts` in the browser's eager module set — a node-only string-replace function in the runtime graph. `ls plugins/` → vite-defer-glass-fonts.ts, vite-source-export.ts (the correct home already exists; no new directory needed).
defects.mechanism: two execution lifetimes in one module → inverted build→app-internals dependency
defects.reproduction: vite.config.ts:15 pulls a demo/ app module into the node build graph; the live `performance.getEntriesByType('resource')` probe shows the reverse edge shipping ground.ts (with injectGroundTokens) to the browser.
defects.proposedCure: Split by lifetime, not feature: demo/shell/boot/ground.contract.ts (constants + buildGroundRecord + normalizeGroundStops, browser only) and plugins/vite-ground-tokens.ts (a `Plugin` exporting `groundRecordInject()`, node only, importing the contract). vite.config.ts then imports from plugins/ like its two siblings and the edge reverses to build → contract, which is legal.

defects.defect: The 14-view route table is duplicated between router/index.ts and viewSchema.ts with no compile-time link; viewSchema.ts's own header states the duplicate was retired (it was not); a masking fallback silently converts drift into a wrong render; and `meta:{admin:true}` is a third, dead encoding of the admin predicate.
defects.evidence: demo/color-picker/router/index.ts:21-38 = 14 bare string literals. demo/shell/viewSchema.ts:35-49 (`ViewId`) + :104-233 (`VIEW_MAP`) = the same 14. viewSchema.ts:7-11 claims the `router/index.ts` copy was retired at D.W3 Lane D; `grep -n "viewSchema\|ViewId" demo/color-picker/router/index.ts` → (no output) — it was not. Masking fallback: demo/shell/useViewManager.ts:43-46 `return isViewId(name) ? name : "picker"`. Dead third encoding: router/index.ts:31-35 carries `meta:{admin:true}`; `grep -rn "meta\.admin\|meta\?\.admin" demo/` → (no output). The live admin predicate is the string prefix at usePaletteWiring.ts:168, usePaneRouter.ts:93 and :140.
defects.mechanism: one concept, three partial untyped homes, drift absorbed by a masking fallback
defects.reproduction: Add `{ path: "/foo", name: "foo", component: Stub }` to router/index.ts and navigate to /#/foo: `isViewId("foo")` is false, `currentView` becomes "picker", the picker renders at a URL claiming otherwise. No error, no warning. (The inverse case is masked by the catch-all at :37 — which is why /#/does-not-exist shows text length 859, identical to /#/, in audit/visual/REPORT.md.)
defects.proposedCure: Derive routes from VIEW_MAP: `...(Object.keys(VIEW_MAP) as ViewId[]).map(id => ({ path: …, name: id, component: Stub }))` plus the catch-all. Delete `meta.admin`. Replace the `?? "picker"` coercion with a router-level redirect (the catch-all already exists) so an unknown name is a navigation event, not a silent substitution.

defects.defect: vue-router is installed but renders nothing (14 null-render Stub components; `<router-view>` appears nowhere), and view→component resolution is a THIRD table — a 10-arm string if-chain that discards the closed unions viewSchema already defines and ends in a masking fallback.
defects.evidence: demo/color-picker/router/index.ts:19 `const Stub = { render: () => null }` used 14×. `grep -rn "router-view\|RouterView" demo/` → one hit, router/index.ts:16, the comment admitting it. demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:81-95 `componentFor(name: string | null)` — a 10-arm if-chain ending `return ColorPicker;` at :94. Its parameter is `string | null` although viewSchema.ts:52-66 defines `LeftPane` and `RightPane` as closed unions and the only callers pass exactly those (usePaneRouter.ts:165, :171).
defects.mechanism: three tables for one lattice, none linked by a type; discarded union forces a masking fallback
defects.reproduction: Add "foo" to the `LeftPane` union and a VIEW_MAP row using it. `tsc` reports nothing — `componentFor("foo")` type-checks and returns ColorPicker at runtime.
defects.proposedCure: Collapse to one table: PaneConfig gains `leftComponent`/`rightComponent` (viewSchema.ts already imports `type { Component }` at :17, so defineAsyncComponent values live there); componentFor becomes a Record keyed by the closed union so tsc proves exhaustiveness; routes derive from the same keys (L-4). Three tables → one; two masking fallbacks die by construction.

defects.defect: App.vue's eager static import graph defeats the async pane split: 20 demo/palettes modules (29 live), including all five admin ports and four admin API modules, load on an anonymous visitor's first paint while AdminPane/PalettesPane/BrowsePane are lazy. The 10-line comment booking this as a known residual rests on a package.json premise that has been false since commit 164343c1.
defects.evidence: Static walker from App.vue: 72 eager modules — `{demo/color-picker:13, demo/color-session:20, demo/palettes:20, demo/platform:10, demo/shell:5, ...}`; the 20 palettes modules include useAdminAudit/useAdminFlagged/useAdminTags/useAdminUsers/useColorNameQueue/useSlugMigration/useVersionHistory/usePalettePorts/palettes/api/index.ts; 10 dynamic-import boundaries found (all ten panes). Live probe on /#/: `totalEagerModules: 238`, `demoDirs: {shell:31, palettes:29, color-session:23, picker:23, ui:11, platform:10, scenes:3, shared:2}`, with palettes/api/admin-audit.ts, admin-colors.ts, admin-palettes.ts, admin-users.ts, dialog/FlagReportDialog.vue, dialog/VersionHistoryDrawer.vue all present. Edges: App.vue:188 → composables/usePaletteWiring.ts:24 → palettes/usePalettePorts.ts (imports :4-19, 15 composables + 3 auth); App.vue:176 → ../palettes/browser/dialog barrel (dialog/index.ts:6-9 re-exports 3 dialogs + a composable) while only MigratePalettesDialog is used. False premise: App.vue:168-175 asserts "the root package.json marks ./demo/** side-effecting"; `python3 -c "import json;print(json.load(open('package.json'))['sideEffects'])"` → `False`; `git log -p -S '"./demo/**"' -- package.json` → the array was replaced at 164343c1 (feat(v4)!).
defects.mechanism: provide-scope conflated with use-scope — root-level DI statically pins every port to the eager chunk regardless of async boundaries
defects.reproduction: Both probes pasted above and in the report: the static walker output and the live `performance.getEntriesByType('resource')` bucketing on http://localhost:9000/#/.
defects.proposedCure: Split providePalettePorts by lifetime and provide each part where it is used: always-on (session/store/paletteActions) from main.ts via `app.provide`; browse ports from BrowsePane.vue; the five admin ports + palettes/api/admin-* from AdminPane.vue — both already async boundaries. usePaletteWiring's four orchestration watchers (:137-171) move to the panes whose ports they bridge; only the genuinely cross-cutting logout rule (:167-171) stays at the shell, needing the session port alone. Import MigratePalettesDialog from its file, or reduce dialog/index.ts to a type barrel. Delete the false 10-line rationale rather than carrying its booked follow-up.

defects.defect: `usePalettePorts` is a god provider: one function constructs and provides fifteen composables, so every injector of any single port pulls the construction of all fifteen — reconstituting at the DI seam the god facade it was created to dissolve.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts:4-19 imports and installs usePaletteStore, useAdminAuth, useUserAuth, useSession, useBrowsePalettes, useAdminUsers, useColorNameQueue, useSlugMigration, usePaletteActions, useFilteredList, useAdminAudit, useAdminFlagged, useAdminTags, useVersionHistory, useTagEdit. usePaletteWiring.ts:1-4 records it "replaced the old usePaletteManager god facade … dissolved into five narrow ports" — the ports are narrow, the installer is not.
defects.mechanism: god module reconstituted at the DI seam after being dissolved into parts
defects.reproduction: L-6's measurement is the reproduction: 15 composables + 4 API modules in the eager graph of a route that mounts none of them.
defects.proposedCure: Same cure as L-6 — there is no separate fix. A provider whose scope equals its constituents' scopes is not a god module; scope each group to the pane that consumes it.

defects.defect: Ownership inversion: the shell reaches into three workbench panes and calls their private methods by name through `any` refs with optional-call, so a rename in a workbench produces a silently dead dock button with no compile error and no runtime error.
defects.evidence: App.vue:317-319 three `ref<any>(null)` (generatePaneRef/gradientPaneRef/mixPaneRef); App.vue:323 and :330 `function onDesktopLeftMount(el: any)` / `onDesktopRightMount(el: any)`. demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:196-222 makes nine duck-typed reaches, each optional-chained on the METHOD: `paneRefs.generate.value?.regenerate?.()`, `.save?.()`, `.copyColors?.()`; `paneRefs.gradient.value?.reset?.()`, `.copyCSS?.()`, `.seedFromPalette?.()`; `paneRefs.mix.value?.clearSelection?.()`, `.startMix?.()`, `.copyResult?.()`. No interface, no type.

defects.reproduction: Rename `regenerate` → `regen` in demo/workbenches/generate/GeneratePane.vue. Demo typecheck passes (the ref is `any`). The dock's Regenerate button becomes a no-op. Nothing reports it.
defects.proposedCure: Invert: `demo/shell/actionBar.ts` exporting `ACTION_BAR_KEY: InjectionKey<Ref<DockActionBar|null>>`; each workbench calls `useProvidedActionBar({label, icon, actions})` in its own setup, naming its own handlers in its own file; the shell injects. usePaneRouter's 40-line actionBar computed (:188-228) deletes entirely; App.vue loses three `any` refs, two mount callbacks, and the paneRefs parameter. `DockActionBar` (already at usePaneRouter.ts:49-58) becomes the real contract instead of a shape three files re-guess.

defects.defect: Two owners of "read the colour out of the URL"; the router-side reader is inert at boot (vue-router's initial navigation is asynchronous, so `route.query` is empty during App setup) and its result is logically subsumed by the hydration source, making the `!appliedFromUrl` guard term unable to change any branch.
defects.evidence: Reader 1: demo/color-picker/composables/boot/hydrate.ts:51-61 hand-parses the hash with URLSearchParams, requires both space+color. Reader 2: demo/color-session/useColorUrl.ts:26-31 reads route.query.space/color, requires both. hydrate.ts:49-50's stated justification ("runs before router installation") is false — index.html:211 `app.use(router)` precedes :212 `app.mount()`, so App setup runs after installation. The real mechanism: node_modules/vue-router/dist/vue-router.js:1462-1466 starts the initial navigation with `push(routerHistory.location)` — a Promise — inside `install`, so `currentRoute.value` is still START_LOCATION_NORMALIZED (query {}) when App's setup runs synchronously inside app.mount(). Hence useColorUrl.ts:70 `const appliedFromUrl = applyUrlToModel()` is false on every cold load. Subsumption: both readers require both params, so appliedFromUrl===true ⟹ hydration.source==="url", and App.vue:378 `if (!appliedFromUrl && hydration.source !== "url")` already gates on the latter.
defects.mechanism: dual ownership of one concept, one instance vestigial after a transposition
defects.reproduction: Deterministic source read, both halves: vue-router.js:1462-1466 (async navigation start) + index.html:210-212 (synchronous mount ordering) + the conjunct-subsumption argument over hydrate.ts:51-61 vs useColorUrl.ts:26-31.
defects.proposedCure: hydrate.ts owns the FIRST value (already correct); useColorUrl owns the LIVE sync only — delete its boot-time applyUrlToModel() call and the appliedFromUrl return, and reduce App.vue:378 to `if (hydration.source !== "url") restoreFromStorage();`. One owner per phase. Correct hydrate.ts:49-50's rationale to the real one (the router's initial navigation is a promise) — that is the fact a future reader needs.

defects.defect: Ownership recorded in prose rather than in types has drifted: three files point at App.vue for watchers it does not contain, and two of App.vue's own structural rationales cite artefacts that no longer exist.
defects.evidence: `grep -c "watch(" demo/color-picker/App.vue` → 0. Yet demo/scenes/blob/BlobPane.vue:9 cites "App.vue's deriveBlobPalette watch" (real owner: boot/useAtmosphere.ts:393) and demo/scenes/atmosphere/aurora-atoms.ts:16-18 cites "App.vue's watch" (real owner: useAtmosphere.ts:143). App.vue's own dead rationales: :168-175 the `./demo/**` sideEffects premise (dead since 164343c1 — see L-6), and :201-206 + :208-210 both order imports "AFTER style.css"; `ls demo/styles/style.css` → No such file or directory (`ls demo/styles/` → animations.css focus-ring.css foundation.css hljs.css shell.css utils.css). The same rename also stranded demo/DESIGN.md, which cites demo/@/styles/style.css line numbers throughout (routed, out of scope here).
defects.mechanism: ownership expressed in prose, not in types — prose does not move when code moves and grep cannot verify it
defects.reproduction: The four commands above: the `grep -c`, the two citing lines, and the `ls`.
defects.proposedCure: Not "fix the comments" — remove the need for them. The cross-file pointers exist because the owner is not discoverable from the type: useAtmosphereBoot returns `{auroraCssGradient, auroraArrived}` while silently provide-ing SAFE_ACCENT_KEY, AURORA_ATOMS_KEY, BLOB_CONFIG_KEY (documented only in App.vue:278-289). Make the provides part of the declared surface and have injection keys carry their producer's name; then the owner is found by go-to-definition and every "App.vue's watch" comment becomes deletable rather than correctable.

defects.defect: A glass-ui primitive removed at 7.0.0 is re-implemented locally inside the demo's dock, complete with a parameter accepted and discarded solely to match the deleted API's signature — a back-compat shim whose purpose is confessed in the comment beside it.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/layers/ActionBarLayer.vue:54-82 (reachable from App.vue:35 via `<Dock>`): header "V-W44 (Glass 7): glass-ui removed the standalone `useLayerTransition` … (Relay note for glass: a public content-swap composable would retire this local shim.)"; :63 `function useLayerTransition(...)`; :67 `void opts.containerEl; // signature parity with the retired producer composable`. Upstream confirmation: `grep -rn useLayerTransition node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/*.d.ts` → (no output) at glass-ui 7.0.0.
defects.mechanism: design-system primitive retired without a successor → consumer re-homes it locally and preserves the dead signature
defects.reproduction: The grep above (absent upstream) plus ActionBarLayer.vue:67 (the discarded parameter).
defects.proposedCure: Two moves, in order: (1) drop `containerEl` from the local signature today — it is dead weight the moment nothing else implements the interface; (2) relay to glass-ui for a public content-swap composable (the standing BH/BI relay fond) and delete the local copy when it lands. Do not leave the parity parameter as a placeholder for a successor that may never arrive.

defects.defect: Two directories are named for the colour picker and the entry is the one that is not the picker — the name signals the inverse of the ownership, which is why shell concerns were filed under the entry's `composables/` instead of demo/shell/.
defects.evidence: vite.config.ts:243 `root: "./demo/color-picker/"` (the application root, holding index.html, App.vue, router/, ErrorBoundary.vue and ten boot composables). App.vue:164 `import { ColorPicker } from "../picker";` → demo/picker/ (the actual feature). Misfiled-by-name consequences: demo/color-picker/composables/boot/* (10 files, ~1500 lines), usePaletteWiring.ts, useDevicePixelSnap.ts — all shell concerns whose siblings (PaneSlot, Dock, useViewManager, usePaneRouter, viewSchema) live in demo/shell/. hydrate.ts:32-40 reaches `../../../color-session/...` — three parent hops out of a directory nominally "the entry".
defects.mechanism: naming collision mis-signalling ownership, driving misfiled modules
defects.reproduction: `ls demo/color-picker demo/picker` — both exist; the entry is the former, the feature the latter.
defects.proposedCure: Rename demo/color-picker/ → demo/app/ (five path updates: vite.config.ts:243, the two @source globs at foundation.css:91-92 collapsing to one, and the two plugins/ references), and move boot/, usePaletteWiring, useDevicePixelSnap, ErrorBoundary.vue into demo/shell/. Do it in the same wave as L-1, since main.ts lands there anyway.

defects.defect: Continuous ambient WebGL motion never terminates and there is no still/pause control, failing both arms of the canon's motion law. Measured still running at 14.6s after load, on mobile included.
defects.evidence: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:145 "Continuous Aurora/Blob ambient motion terminates within five seconds or exposes one persistent keyboard-operable still/pause control whose state is announced and remembered. Paused, parked and offscreen mean no animation work." App.vue:285-289 mounts the atmosphere renderer and App.vue:9-17 owns its canvas, so the control has no other home. (The reduced-motion arm IS satisfied — rafPer1500ms=0 under reducedMotion:reduce, STATES.json — but an OS preference is not the persistent, announced, remembered control §6 demands.)
defects.mechanism: an unbounded ambient renderer with no user-facing lifecycle seam; the overture DAG exposes beats to START motion and nothing to stop it
defects.reproduction: node <scratchpad>/probe-overture.mjs  → per-matrix `rafRate_last6s` field: 261.0/s, 284.0/s, 259.5/s, all sampled from t=8.5s to t=14.6s post-load. Then grep for any pause mechanism → none.
defects.proposedCure: One shell-level ambient-motion control, keyboard-operable with `aria-pressed`, persisted alongside the color-mode store, gating BOTH renderers through the OVERTURE_KEY beats App.vue already provides — so "paused" tears the rAF loops down rather than merely zeroing opacity, satisfying §6's "Paused, parked and offscreen mean no animation work."

defects.defect: App.vue's boot contract is split across a file it does not own and duplicated in two languages. It mounts onto `<body>` as a three-root fragment, depends on three host attributes declared in index.html (one of which is provably dead), makes the canon's required static boot-error region structurally impossible to preserve, and re-runs the prepaint script's URL/storage/default precedence a second time in TypeScript — which §6.2 forbids in those words.
defects.evidence: Measured (probe-app-D.mjs, all three matrices): mountHostIsBody=true, appLayoutParent="body", bodyAttrs=`class="relative" id="app" data-paper-field="" data-v-app=""`, groundState=null. The mount is demo/color-picker/index.html:205-213 (MT-F012's P0 inline module) ending `app.mount("#app")`, and `#app` IS `<body>` (index.html:226). App.vue is a 3-root fragment: div.app-layout (:2), comment nodes (:144-149), MigratePalettesDialog (:152). (1) `class="relative"` is DEAD: the atmosphere canvas (App.vue:9-17, `absolute inset-0`) is a descendant of `.app-layout` (App.vue:2) which is already `position: relative` (shell.css:25), so the nearest positioned ancestor is never `<body>` — a legacy positioning ancestor, owner edict 2. (2) `data-paper-field` is glass-ui's field contract governing App.vue's own descendants incl. portalled dialogs (index.html:222-226) yet is declared where App.vue cannot see it. (3) Mount replaces the host's children, so `<body>` can hold no `<noscript>` and no pre-rendered fallback — while VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:168 requires "A static semantic boot-error region already present in HTML becomes visible through that data state"; measured groundState=null confirms the whole §6.2 latch (data-ground-state / -schema / -store) is unimplemented. (4) index.html:180-200 runs URL/storage/default precedence in vanilla JS writing --saved-bg-0..N; App.vue:231 `resolveHydratedBootModel()` runs URL->storage->default AGAIN in TypeScript (boot/hydrate.ts:53-78) — VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:172: "The hydrated model consumes the frozen boot object ...; it does not repeat scheme/URL/storage precedence, reconstruct an initial palette in TypeScript, or repaint a second 'equivalent' ground."
defects.mechanism: split root ownership — the component's own root contract (positioning ancestor, material attribute, boot precedence) lives in the entry HTML, so it is untyped, untestable, invisible to the component, and duplicated
defects.reproduction: node <scratchpad>/probe-app-D.mjs  → every row: mountHostIsBody true, appLayoutParent "body", bodyAttrs 'class="relative" id="app" data-paper-field=""', groundState null. Then read index.html:205-213 (mount), :222-226 (data-paper-field rationale), :180-200 (prepaint precedence) against boot/hydrate.ts:53-78 (the second precedence engine).
defects.proposedCure: Take MT-F012's cure and finish it. Move the 8 lines to main.ts referenced via `src=`, with `<div id="app">` as the host. Then: `.app-layout` becomes the app's own root and already declares position:relative, so `class="relative"` is DELETED not moved; `data-paper-field` moves onto `.app-layout` — the element App.vue owns and documents; `<body>` regains the right to carry §6.2's static boot-error region and a `<noscript>`; and main.ts becomes the single reader of the frozen `window.__VALUE_GROUND_BOOT__`, handing it to `createApp(App, { boot })` so App.vue CONSUMES the boot object as §6.2 requires and `resolveHydratedBootModel`'s duplicate precedence engine is deleted outright rather than kept in sync. Necessary but insufficient: it does not fix the 3-root fragment, D-2, D-3 or D-4.

defects.defect: "Not found" has no designed state: an unknown route silently redirects to `/` with no announced reason, rendering byte-identical content to the home route. The canon requires the redirect reason in one polite status plus the destination title/H1.
defects.evidence: demo/color-picker/router/index.ts:37 `{ path: "/:pathMatch(.*)*", redirect: "/" }`. Measured in the tracked matrix: REPORT.md:133 `/#/does-not-exist` text=859 vs REPORT.md:119 `/#/` text=859 — identical, in all four matrices (REPORT.md:133,148,163,178). The shell mounts no polite status region — its only live region is ErrorBoundary's role="alert" / aria-live="assertive" (ErrorBoundary.vue:6,20), which is assertive and reserved for render throws — and there is no H1 to focus (D-4).
defects.mechanism: a state elided rather than designed — the router expresses the recovery (redirect) but not the communication (status + identity), so the app silently rewrites the user's intent

defects.proposedCure: One shell-owned polite status region (`role="status"`, `aria-live="polite"`) beside the H1, written by the same route-settlement commit installDocumentTitle already hooks (router/index.ts:47). The 404 becomes an announced redirect rather than a silent rewrite.

defects.defect: Two statements of business logic inside an inline template handler, mutating a foreign composable's ref directly, with a bare magic index — and the state it mutates is the very left/right view state the canon retires. It also fires on desktop where it is meaningless, and on mobile the other half of the same expression is a no-op.
defects.evidence: App.vue:41-42: `@commit-edit="colorPickerRef?.commitEdit(); viewManager.mobilePaneIndex.value = 1"` and `@cancel-edit="colorPickerRef?.cancelEdit(); viewManager.mobilePaneIndex.value = 1"`. Three faults: sequenced statements in a template expression; a foreign composable's ref mutated from the template rather than through its API; the literal `1` as an unnamed index meaning "the right pane". It runs on desktop where mobilePaneIndex is meaningless, and per D-1 `colorPickerRef` is null on mobile so on the one viewport where the index matters the `commitEdit()` half never fires. `mobilePaneIndex` is itself the state VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:89 retires. Owner edicts 3 (KISS) and 7 (idiomatic Vue 3.5).
defects.mechanism: logic leaking into the template because the composable exposes raw state instead of named intents
defects.reproduction: Read App.vue:41-42 ; grep -n 'mobilePaneIndex' demo/shell/useViewManager.ts and demo/color-picker/App.vue ; VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:89.
defects.proposedCure: `viewManager` exposes a named intent (`returnToInspector()`); the handler becomes one method call and the magic index becomes a named position inside the composable. Under D-2 the state disappears.

defects.defect: `any` throughout the shell's ref plumbing erases the real public shapes of the three pane instances, which is the direct enabling condition for D-1: the null-safe call chain type-checks forever, so the missing mobile `:on-mount` produced no diagnostic anywhere.

The erased shapes are real and enumerated at usePaneRouter.ts:196-222 — regenerate, save, copyColors, reset, copyCSS, seedFromPalette, clearSelection, startMix, copyResult. `paneRefs.generate.value?.regenerate?.()` type-checks against `null` indefinitely. (The file otherwise honours verbatimModuleSyntax correctly — all type-only imports are `import type`, App.vue:163.)
defects.mechanism: type erasure at a DI seam — `any` at the boundary converts a structural wiring error into a silent runtime no-op
defects.reproduction: grep -n 'ref<any>\|: any' demo/color-picker/App.vue → :317,318,319,323,330 ; grep -n 'onMount' demo/shell/PaneSlot.vue → :52 ; then usePaneRouter.ts:196 shows the erased call.

defects.defect: A cold load / refresh / shared link on any route whose left pane is not the color-picker (10 of 14 routes) permanently stalls the overture beat DAG at B2: overture:b3 and overture:b4 never fire for the life of the session, and the picker's hero-blob ornament (v-if gated on b4) never mounts again on ANY route thereafter.
defects.evidence: Measured with an isolated Chromium probe against localhost:9000. CONTROL cold-load /#/ → marks [b0,b1,b3,b2,b4], `.hero-blob-anchor` present. DEEPLINK /#/generate → marks [b0,b1,b2] only, blob absent; after hash-nav to /#/ still [b0,b1,b2], `.picker-shell` present but blob STILL absent. Identical for /#/browse. First-pane oracle (pre-navigation MutationObserver) on cold /#/generate records `picker-shell` as the FIRST mounted left pane before the GeneratePane. Code: App.vue:90 and App.vue:109 are the ONLY call sites of overture.noteLeftPlateSettled (grep), both via PaneSlot.vue:118 `@after-appear`; useViewManager.ts:43-46 falls back to "picker" while route.name is undefined; PaneSlot.vue:74 seeds liveComponent at setup; useOverture.ts:153-183 gates b4 on b3Complete.
defects.mechanism: State derived from a source of truth that is not yet true: index.html:205-213 mounts without awaiting router.isReady(), so the first render uses the picker config; PaneSlot then swaps the child (router resolution + the deliberate one-rAF commit at PaneSlot.vue:95), which cancels Vue's `appear` transition so @after-appear never fires. B3 is the one beat in this boot chain with NO state-checked fallback (contrast useDockArrival.ts:63-72 and useOverture.ts:173), so one missed DOM event is terminal.
defects.reproduction: node <scratchpad>/probe-b3.mjs — launches chromium 1440x900, goto http://localhost:9000/#/generate (or /#/browse), wait 5s, read performance marks + `.hero-blob-anchor`; then set location.hash='#/', wait 7s, re-read. Compare against goto('/#/'). Deep links yield 3 marks and no blob; the control yields 5 marks and a blob.
defects.proposedCure: Take the MT-F012 entry cure and make it the idiomatic vue-router SPA boot: in the new main.ts do `app.use(router); await router.isReady(); app.mount('#app')`. With the route true at first render the first-mounted left pane is the final one, its appear completes, B3 and B4 fire. Second, independent arm: arm B3 on the left pane's MOUNT plus a getAnimations() settle check (the sibling beats' idiom) instead of a single Transition appear event.

defects.proposedCure: Delete the two currentConfig-name dispatchers. PaneSlot already owns `liveKey`: have it call `onMount(instance, liveKey)` and let App store into one `paneRefs` record keyed by pane name — one path for mobile and both desktop slots, with the slot (not a second source of truth) answering 'which ref'. defects.defect: The ref-capture callback fills the WRONG ref for one frame during a pane swap (a ColorPicker instance lands in generatePaneRef while colorPickerRef is nulled), and it re-fires on every unrelated parent re-render.
defects.evidence: jsdom repro using this repo's own vue, modelling the exact PaneSlot↔App contract (inline arrow :ref, one-rAF commit, `left === '…' ? el : null` dispatcher). Trace: after the config flip and before the rAF commit → `left=generate el=Picker -> picker=null generate=Picker`; one unrelated parent re-render → the callback fires again with the same instance. Code: App.vue:323-332 reads currentConfig.value.left (the incoming view) while PaneSlot.vue:86-97 delays the rendered triplet by one rAF; PaneSlot.vue:124 builds a fresh arrow `:ref` on every render; App.vue:317-319 declare `ref<any>` so no type error is possible.
defects.mechanism: Two sources of truth for one identity: 'what is mounted' (the slot's liveKey) vs 'what the route says' (currentConfig.left), read in the window where they disagree. The `any` typing plus `?.method?.()` optional calls convert a wrong-instance assignment into silence rather than a TypeError.
defects.reproduction: node <scratchpad>/ref-churn.mjs (jsdom + vue) — prints the callback trace; line `left=generate el=Picker -> picker=null generate=Picker` is the mis-assignment.
defects.proposedCure: Same as C-2: PaneSlot emits (instance, key); App keys the record off that name. Additionally hoist PaneSlot's `:ref` to a stable function so Vue stops re-running it on every parent-driven update.

defects.defect: `import { ColorPicker } from "../picker"` is used only in a type position but is not `import type` — a verbatimModuleSyntax (edict 8) violation that emits a runtime import for a type.

defects.defect: Every boot rewrites the address bar with a colour the user never picked, violating the hydrate.ts 'born hydrated, ONE commit' law App.vue's own comment asserts.
defects.evidence: Clean browser context (empty localStorage) loading http://localhost:9000/#/generate settles at http://localhost:9000/#/generate?space=lab&color=lab(92%25+88.8+20+/+82.7%25) — measured in every isolated probe run. Mechanism code: useColorPipeline.ts:50-52 unconditionally re-assigns model.value at setup (clampColorToSpaceDomain returns a fresh object; the `if (model.value.color)` guard is always true), tripping the identity-based watcher at useColorUrl.ts:79-82 → router.replace. App.vue:245 then :377 fix the composition order; App.vue:369-376 claims the opposite ('an idempotent re-commit').
defects.mechanism: An identity-changing write performed for a value-level clamp, observed by an identity-based watcher — the boot commits a URL write no user action requested.
defects.reproduction: node <scratchpad>/probe-app.mjs (fresh context per run) — read `location.href` after load; it always carries ?space=&color= even with empty storage and a bare hash.
defects.proposedCure: Make the boot clamp a no-op write: compare the clamped colour to the incoming one and skip the assignment when nothing changed (or clamp inside hydrate before the ref exists, which is where the ordering law already says the first value is decided).

result.addendumClause:
## ADDENDUM — App shell: the composition root, the one lattice, and the producer housing

**Normative.** The value.js demo has no composition root, and every structural defect in
`demo/color-picker/App.vue` is downstream of that fact or of one adjacent fact: the shell hand-rolls
a housing primitive glass-ui already ships.

1. **The entry is a module, not markup.** `demo/app/main.ts` is the sole composition root. It
   performs, in order: the one stylesheet import (`../styles/foundation.css`), `initGlobalDark()`,
   `createApp(App, { boot: window.__VALUE_GROUND_BOOT__ })`, `app.use(router)`,
   **`await router.isReady()`**, the app-level `provide`s (API client, always-on session ports),
   and `app.mount("#app")`. `demo/app/index.html` contains **zero inline executable script**: one
   external classic prepaint (`./prepaint.js`) and one external module (`./main.ts`). No component
   may perform app-level installs, import a stylesheet, or assume mount order. The `await
   router.isReady()` is normative, not stylistic: without it the first-rendered scene is not the
   final scene on 10 of 14 routes and the overture DAG stalls at B2 for the life of the session.

2. **The mount container is not the portal host.** `<body class="relative" data-paper-field>` keeps
   **both** attributes — they serve the body-portalled dialogs, which are the app root's siblings —
   and Vue receives its own `<div id="app">`. Exactly one attribute (`id`) moves. Proposals to
   delete `class="relative"` or relocate `data-paper-field` onto `.app-layout` are refused: one
   `position:absolute` direct child of `<body>` uses body as its containing block, and the field
   stamp must dominate four sibling portal hosts.

3. **`groundRecordInject`, `__GROUND_*__` and the TypeScript precedence engine die in one cut.**
   Per §6.2 the prepaint is an external classic script with no build-time token injection; the
   scheme defaults are canonical tokens in `--ground-seed-token-light` / `-dark`. `vite.config.ts`
   imports nothing under `demo/`. `boot/ground.ts` and `boot/hydrate.ts` are deleted; the app
   consumes the frozen boot object and never re-derives URL→storage→default. `useColorUrl` owns the
   live sync only.

4. **One route lattice.** `demo/shell/viewSchema.ts` is the single table. Routes derive from its
   keys; scene resolution is a `Record` over the closed union; dock metadata reads the same rows.
   `meta.admin` (five producers, zero consumers), the fourteen literal route rows, the
   `isViewId(name) ? name : "picker"` coercion and `componentFor`'s `return ColorPicker` catch-all
   are deleted. An unknown view is a navigation event, never a substituted render.

5. **Region composition is the producer's.** glass-ui 7.0.0 exports `InstrumentChassis` with
   `proportion: "golden" | "preview-dominant"`, `reserve`, a typed `boundaries` set, `#stage` /
   `#inspector` / `#action` slots, inspector-absent expansion, and a container-query collapse. Per
   `OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md` §5 seam 1, **value.js owns the route `<main>` and adds no grid
   CSS**. `.pane-container`, `.pane-container--dual`, `.pane-wrapper--left/--right/--ghost`, the
   `[data-layout]` display witnesses, the breakpoint `v-if` mount fork, `mobilePaneIndex`,
   `PaneSegmentedControl.vue` and `PaneSlot.vue` are deleted, not restyled. The shell's block axis
   becomes `min-height: 100dvh` with a sticky dock band; the document scrolls.

6. **The edge points down.** No shell module may name a leaf component's method. Workbenches publish
   their own action bar through `ACTION_BAR_KEY` (`demo/shell/actionBar.ts`); the shell injects.
   `usePaneRouter.ts` is deleted whole. `providePalettePorts` is split by lifetime — always-on ports
   at `main.ts`, browse ports at `BrowsePane.vue`, admin ports at `AdminPane.vue`. A provider whose
   scope exceeds its consumers' scope is a god module and is refused.

7. **The shell owns identity, not just landmarks.** One `<h1>` inside `<main>`, fed by the same
   route identity `installDocumentTitle` composes; a skip link as the first tabbable node; one
   `role="status" aria-live="polite"` region beside the H1 for redirect reasons; `tabindex="-1"` on
   `<main>`. The shell mounts no domain dialogs: storage recovery renders inside the Library's
   `<main>` per §7.

8. **Beats carry terminal arms.** No beat may be armed by a single DOM event without a
   state-checked floor (`getAnimations()`, the idiom `useDockArrival.ts:58-72` already proves). B4
   gains a terminal `unavailable` arm (context lost, WebGL absent, chunk rejected) and the blob
   gains the `webglcontextlost`/`webglcontextrestored` contract the aurora already has; on
   `unavailable` the headline interval collapses to the named shared section rhythm.

9. **Ambient motion has a lifecycle seam.** One shell-level, keyboard-operable, `aria-pressed`,
   persisted still/pause control gating both renderers through `OVERTURE_KEY`. Paused means the rAF
   loops are torn down, not opacity-zeroed.

10. **Design-system successors are composed, never re-implemented.** `DockCrossfade` ships at
    glass-ui 7.0.0; the local `useLayerTransition` and its `void opts.containerEl` parity parameter
    are deleted in the same wave. This clause is the standing answer to every "relay for a
    successor" bank: run the grep first.

**Execution order (binding).** `V·MT-W-ARCH-1` (entry + lattice) → `V·MT-W-ARCH-2` (action-bar
inversion) → `V·MT-W-ARCH-3` (single-scene shell + identity + scroll) → `V·MT-W-ARCH-4` (terminal
beats + non-vacuous oracles) → `V·MT-W-ARCH-5` (DI scope, gated against `dist/`, which requires
W-ARCH-1). The eleven member compositions FOLD to W18/W19/W24/W26/W27 with row ids `D-2`, `D-3`,
`D-7`, `D-10`, `D-12` preserved; storage recovery FOLDs to W22 as `D-14`. No row is re-booked.
result.dissent:
AGAINST CHALLENGE-D, ON SHAPE (not evidence). D's gestalt — "the cure is a transposition, not a sequence of patches" — is correct about the premise and wrong about the unit of work. Eleven member compositions onto InstrumentChassis is an arc, and FORMATION-LAW L-1 exists precisely because this repository has landed 380 of 1,005 commitments (38%) and the standing 193-wave formation sits at 3 of 199 (2%). Authoring D-2's cure as one wave would produce the thirteenth arc wearing a wave's name. I split it: the shell half (deleting the grid CSS, the mount fork, the ghost slot, mobilePaneIndex, PaneSegmentedControl.vue, PaneSlot.vue) is one completable wave; the eleven members FOLD to the waves OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md §6 already names as their owners. I expect JUROR-3 to weigh this against D's framing.

AGAINST CHALLENGE-L, ON EVIDENCE DISCIPLINE. L's strongest structural finding (the eager palette-ports graph) is measured with an instrument structurally blind to the property claimed: dev-server `performance.getEntriesByType('resource')` counts as a bundle claim. The dev server serves unbundled ESM, so every static import is a separate resource by construction. The finding survives on its static half — `providePalettePorts` is CALLED at the root, so its fifteen constituents are reachable-and-invoked and untree-shakeable at any setting — but the number 238 does not, and a wave inheriting it as a baseline would author a gate it cannot make RED against `dist/`. Compounding: today's built artifact has no application in it (MT-F012), so the correct gate cannot even open until W-ARCH-1 lands. I record that ordering as an explicit edge, not a deferral. FORMATION-LAW L-12 is not decoration.

AGAINST CHALLENGE-C AND CHALLENGE-D TOGETHER, ON THE ROOT CONTRACT. C-8 and D-9 independently reach the same conclusion — that App.vue's root contract must be repatriated from index.html — and both are wrong on two of three arms, in the same direction. I measured: `<body>` has one `position:absolute` direct child (so `class="relative"` is a live containing block, not dead weight) and four teleport hosts that are `.app-layout`'s SIBLINGS (so `data-paper-field` cannot move onto `.app-layout` without re-arming the producer's orphan-card field-floor for every portalled dialog). A wave executing either cure verbatim would break both. The split root contract is real; two thirds of the split are correct, and the correct cut is exactly one attribute (`id`) wide. This is the dissent I most want preserved, because two independent seats agreeing is exactly the condition under which an unmeasured cure gets executed.

CORRECTION OF RECORD, NOT DISSENT. None of the three challengers established the fact that decides the architecture: glass-ui 7.0.0 exports `InstrumentChassis` on a published subpath, ships its CSS (golden = 61.8033989fr/38.1966011fr, preview-dominant = 66.6666667fr/33.3333333fr, a `@container (max-width: 44.9375rem)` single-column collapse, `data-reserve` with two reserve properties, and a typed boundary set), and the demo uses it exactly zero times. D quoted the canon's requirement; I measured the primitive. That reclassifies the shell from "wrong proportions" to "a dual path against a shipping producer primitive", which makes the transposition mandatory under edict 2 rather than aspirational under the constitution — and, decisively, makes it EXECUTABLE today. Likewise, the `useLayerTransition` relay-cure is refuted by a one-line grep (`DockCrossfade` is exported at 7.0.0), which is the same failure mode FORMATION-LAW L-4 was written from.

NO DISSENT ON SEVERITY. All three challengers found real defects on their axis; both BLOCKERs reproduce against today's tree; the premise of guilt was, this time, correct.

waveSpec.title: The shell tells the truth about what it mounted
waveSpec.scope:
demo/color-picker/ (entry, App.vue, composables/boot/*), demo/shell/ (PaneSlot.vue, useViewManager.ts, usePaneRouter.ts, viewSchema.ts, dock/), demo/styles/shell.css + the overture.css relocation, vite.config.ts (entry + ground seam), e2e/smoke/oracles/o4-order-invariance.spec.ts, docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/states.mjs. OUT OF SCOPE, FOLDED BY NAME: the eleven per-member InstrumentChassis compositions and their ratios belong to W18 by VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:56, which requires W18 to ratify one low-fidelity and one real-rendered composition per member before feature styling proceeds. This wave lands the SEAM (the shell stops owning ratio, stage/inspector split, breakpoint mount fork and domain dialogs); W18 lands the VALUES. Five cuts in dependency order: (1) main.ts with `app.use(router); await router.isReady(); app.mount("#app")` and `
`, App.vue dropping both app-level installs and all four CSS imports; (2) PaneSlot reports (instance, liveKey) from a stable non-inline :ref at every call site, then ACTION_BAR_KEY inverts the direction so panes publish and the shell injects, deleting usePaneRouter's 40-line actionBar computed and three ref; (3) the shell owns one

fed by installDocumentTitle's route identity, a skip link as its first tabbable node, and one role=status aria-live=polite region that announces the 404 redirect; (4) .app-layout becomes min-height:100dvh with a sticky dock band so the document scrolls, the shell stops declaring grid-template-columns, and the v-if mount fork / pane-wrapper--left|--right / --ghost / mobilePaneIndex die together with container queries carrying the reflow; (5) routes derive from VIEW_MAP with componentFor keyed by the closed unions (both masking fallbacks die by construction), providePalettePorts splits by lifetime across main.ts/BrowsePane/AdminPane, B4 gains a terminal `unavailable` arm and the blob gains the context-loss contract useAtmosphere.ts:288-301 already models, one aria-pressed still control tears the rAF loops down, overture.css moves to demo/styles/ (a move, never a deletion), injectGroundTokens RETIRES per VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:172, and the residue clears (picker-shell, useClipboard subpath, useColorUrl's vestigial boot read, the useLayerTransition parity parameter, `import type { ColorPicker }`, the three dead rationales, and the real writer of the boot URL rewrite).

result.addendumClause: **V·§App-shell — route truth, slot truth, and shell identity.** The application entry is a module file. It installs the router, awaits `router.isReady()`, and only then mounts; no component may render a route-derived pane before the route is true, and no boot beat may be armed by a single DOM event without a state-checked floor. Pane-instance registration is reported by the slot that mounted the instance, never dispatched by a name a call site guesses; a slot that renders a pane registers it at every viewport, and a control the dock renders as named and enabled is live at every viewport or it is not rendered. The shell owns its route's sole `<main>`, exactly one `<h1>`, one bypass link as its first tabbable node, and one polite status region; it does not own a ratio, a stage/inspector split, a breakpoint mount fork, or any domain dialog. The document is the scroller. No masking fallback may stand between a lattice table and its consumer: unknown names are navigation events, not silent substitutions. Every one of these obligations is discharged by an executable gate that is RED against the tree it was written for; a gate with no input that reddens it is deleted, not weakened.
result.dissent:
AGAINST CHALLENGE-D, ON SEVERITY AND SCOPE. D-2 is upheld — the canon retires the two-pane workspace in five clauses and I read all five. But D-2's framing, that "every finding except D-5, D-6, D-9 and D-14 is a consequence of that one premise, which is why the cure is a transposition", does not survive the measurements. The two defects that actually break the product for a real user are NOT consequences of the two-pane premise. J-1 breaks on /#/gradient at any viewport, dual-pane or single, and would survive the single-scene transposition untouched because its cause is `router.isReady()` and an unfloored beat. J-2 would be MASKED by removing the breakpoint fork, not cured — the per-call-site `:on-mount` prop and the `any`-typed `currentConfig.left` dispatcher would still be there waiting for the next branch. Adjudicating this component as "the architecture is retired, therefore transpose" would ship a beautiful single-scene shell with a wedged boot DAG and a dead dock on mobile. Cut 1 and Cut 2 come first for that reason, and they are the two cuts that need no W18 ratification to land.

AGAINST CHALLENGE-D, ON EVIDENCE DISCIPLINE. Four of its sub-claims are refuted by bytes: D-15's "solid source-side fact" (foundation.css:678-695 contains .atmosphere-canvas at :683 and [data-glass-field-canvas] at :684, and my Chromium forced-colors run shows the shell chrome transforming correctly); D-13's verbatimModuleSyntax parenthetical (App.vue:164); D-12's API-violation charge (useViewManager.ts:59-70 — mobilePaneIndex is a writable computed, its setter IS the API); and D-9's URL-duplication arm (the prepaint script contains no URL read at all). Four refuted sub-claims in one report is the cost of arriving from a premise of guilt, and correcting it is what this seat exists for.

AGAINST CHALLENGE-C, ON C-7. The measurement is right and the mechanism is wrong. A cure written against the stated mechanism ("make the boot clamp a no-op write") would have landed, looked green on inspection, and left the address bar still rewriting — because useColorPipeline's clamp runs at App.vue:245, before useColorUrl's non-immediate watch is installed at App.vue:377. I have gated the observable instead and made "find the real writer" an explicit obligation of the wave.

AGAINST CHALLENGE-L, ON L-3'S CURE. Relocating `injectGroundTokens` to `plugins/vite-ground-tokens.ts` is the right shape of fix for the wrong tranche: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:172 retires `groundRecordInject` and `__GROUND_*__` BY NAME, in the same cut as the frozen boot object. Building the plugin would be building something the canon has already scheduled for demolition. The finding stands; the cure is retirement, folded into J-9.

WHERE I EXPECT THE OTHER JURORS TO DISAGREE WITH ME, AND MY POSITION. I graded J-5 (the retired architecture) BLOCKER but split its disposition BUILD + FOLD(W18), and I graded J-6 (50/50) MAJOR rather than BLOCKER. A design-axis juror will likely grade both BLOCKER and demand they land whole in this wave. I hold that VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:56 settles it against them: W18 must ratify one low-fidelity and one real-rendered composition PER MEMBER — "Picker cannot stand in for About" — before feature styling proceeds. This wave can honestly land the seam and exactly one ratified value (Picker's exact golden inspector 38.1966011%, :42) and no more. A wave that promised eleven compositions would be promising W18's work with W18's authority, and its gate would be unwritable — which is the same failure mode as a vacuous gate, arriving from the other direction.

TWO GATES I REFUSED TO WRITE, ON PURPOSE. A forced-colors gate would be GREEN at authorship (DIS-1) and is therefore vacuous. A blob-determinism gate would be flaky rather than sound, because I cannot name an input that reliably reddens it (HYP-2: both of my Chromium /#/ desktop runs produced the blob; the one tracked WebKit absence is a real context loss, not a demonstrated rate). Under born-RED law both must be deleted rather than weakened, and I deleted them. What survives from HYP-2 and IS gated is the byte-certain half: the blob has no context-loss contract anywhere in the tree, and B4 has only a success edge.

ONE UNSOUND GATE I FOUND IN MY OWN SUITE AND FIXED. G1b originally selected on `.picker-shell` — a token J-20 deletes. It would have gone RED after the wave because its own selector retired, not because the contract broke. Rewritten to assert "5 overture marks + ornament present" and re-verified RED. I own the gate soundness of this spec and that is what owning it looks like.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure beneath `demo/color-session/ColorSpaceSelector.vue`: module boundaries, unique semantic ownership, direction of dependency, and the published public surface.
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M context). Declared explicitly at spawn by the orchestrating workflow and confirmed in this seat's environment block. The seat is declared, not inherited; no defect on the model-receipt axis.
result.strongestDefect: L-1 (the color-space catalog has four independent homes — 18/13/11/9 members — with this component owning the superset and every downstream consumer masking its shortfall), with L-16 as its root cause: value.js owns the color-space domain as *types* (`SpaceId`, `CssColorSpace`) and withholds it as *values* (`CSS_COLOR_SPACES` is private at `src/css/grammar.ts:161`; no space registry, no label table, no channel table is exported), so the demo materialised four catalogs, five precision rules and two hand-copied space-sets to fill the gap. Consequence, reproduced live: selecting "Display P3" in this component makes the About pane render CIE RGB's 1931 card — wrong definition, wrong white point, wrong creation year, wrong conversion graph — under a correct "Display P3" heading, with `npm run typecheck` green.
result.negativeProof: The half of the axis that is SOUND, proved rather than assumed: (1) Zero deep-`src/` reach anywhere in the demo — `grep -rn '@src\|from "\(\.\./\)*src/' demo/` returns no output; the T.W1 demo-dogfood keystone holds tree-wide. (2) The component's entire transitive library surface is exactly two published subpaths, `@mkbabb/value.js/color` (`picker-color.ts:27`) and `@mkbabb/value.js/css` (`:34`), both present in `package.json#exports` (`:22`, `:30`); `npx tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --traceResolution` shows `/css` resolving through the real self-package `exports` map to `dist/subpaths/css.d.ts` — a real npm consumer could write both specifiers verbatim, so there is NO false proof of the public API in this component's import graph. (3) `verbatimModuleSyntax` clean: four `import type` statements across the closure plus legal inline `type` specifiers in `picker-color.ts`. (4) None of the challenge's named historical suspects is present — no local `useLayerTransition` reimplementation, no `palettes/export.ts` reach, no third `useDark` store. (5) The `demo/ui/` barrel carries no measurable bundle cost: `esbuild --bundle --minify` gives 14,441 B via the root barrel vs 13,397 B via `@mkbabb/glass-ui/select` — 1,044 B (7.8 %), not the 12× the raw 68-file/225,743-B static graph suggests; `sideEffects: ["*.css"]` shakes correctly, so L-4 stands on structure alone. (6) The scoped style block (`:169-311`) — the `--space-title-ink` ladder, em-relative caret, `--type-display-2` rung, hover-underline register, focus-visible ring — is genuinely well-owned and is implicated in no finding; no animation or keyframe is touched by any proposed cure.

defects.defect: The catalog of "which color spaces exist" has FOUR independent homes with 18 / 13 / 11 / 9 members. This component owns the superset and drives all four; every downstream consumer covers its shortfall with a masking fallback, an `as any`, or a `v-if`. Five of the 18 offered spaces have no `colorSpaceInfo` row; seven have no markdown doc.
defects.evidence: Homes: `demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:72` PICKER_SPACE_NAMES (17) → `color-model.ts:75` DISPLAY_COLOR_SPACE_NAMES (18, read at ColorSpaceSelector.vue:150); `demo/color-session/colorSpaceInfo.ts:18` (13); `demo/scenes/about/AboutPane.vue:79` type MarkdownSpace (11); `demo/color-session/color-space-meta.ts:26` INTERPOLATION_SPACES (9). Masks: `ColorNutritionLabel.vue:210-215` `: colorSpaceInfo.rgb`; `ConsoleRail.vue:174` `(colorSpaceInfo as any)[space]`; `AboutPane.vue:51` `v-if="activeMarkdownModule"`. Measured cross-table: srgb-linear / display-p3 / a98-rgb / prophoto-rgb / rec2020 present in PICKER_SPACE_NAMES, absent from BOTH other tables. Live page text after selecting Display P3: "About the color spaces, Display P3 … Definition: A color space based on the additive mixture of red, green, and blue light. White Point: Varies (typically D65). Gamut: Limited (device-specific). Created: 1931. Conversion Graph RGB→XYZ RGB→Kelvin RGB→HSL RGB→Hex". Screenshots: probe-display-p3-about.png (this directory) and scratchpad/after-display-p3.png (independent 2nd-seat capture).
defects.mechanism: Unique semantic ownership violated four ways. A label table (`PICKER_SPACE_NAMES`) sits inside a math module wedged between PICKER_CHANNELS and buildColor, so it could not be the key set per-space CONTENT is written against; every content surface therefore grew its own enumeration. Nothing in the type system relates them — one is a frozen Record, one an object literal, one a hand-written string union, one an array — so no gate can see a gap. The masking fallbacks then convert the gap into confident misinformation instead of a visible failure.
defects.reproduction: `node scratchpad/repro2.mjs` — chromium 1440×900 → http://localhost:9000/#/ → click `[aria-label="Select color space"]` → click the "Display P3" option. Also reproduced independently by the first pass via scratchpad/chL-css-probe.mjs at 1600×1000. Both hosts' titles read "Display P3"; the entire nutrition card beneath reads CIE RGB 1931; the "Detailed Guide" section renders nothing (`contains 'Oh snap': false`).
defects.proposedCure: Architectural transposition, not gap-filling. (1) The LIBRARY gains the space registry it already half-owns: export from `src/subpaths/color.ts` a mapped type `SPACES: { readonly [S in SpaceId]: SpaceDescriptor<S> }` carrying `id · label · cssSerializable · channels`. A mapped type over `SpaceId` IS exhaustiveness-checked, so adding a space fails the library build until its descriptor exists; this retires PICKER_SPACE_NAMES, PICKER_CHANNELS and both CSS_*_SPACES sets. (2) The DEMO keeps exactly one product layer, `color-session/space-catalog.ts`: `DisplayColorSpace = SpaceId | "hex"` and one `Record<DisplayColorSpace, SpaceDoc>` carrying the prose and the doc loader — a Record over the same union the selector enumerates, so the 5-space and 7-space holes become COMPILE ERRORS. `colorSpaceInfo.ts`, `color-space-meta.ts`, `AboutPane.vue:79-98` and all three masks delete.

defects.defect: `CSS_PICKER_SPACES` is a byte-for-byte copy — identical members AND identical line-wrapping — of `CSS_COLOR_SPACES`, a constant that lives inside the library and is deliberately NOT exported. The subject component branches its entire display policy on the copy, and the drift is structurally invisible to `npm run typecheck`.
defects.evidence: Three homes for one fact: `src/css/types.ts:6-8` (the TYPE authority, 13 members); `src/css/grammar.ts:161-164` `const CSS_COLOR_SPACES = new Set<CssColorSpace>([...])` — private, consumed at `grammar.ts:290`; `demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:92-96` `CSS_PICKER_SPACES` — the copy, read at `ColorSpaceSelector.vue:161`. `docs/tranches/V/ARCHITECTURE.md` states the governing principle verbatim for the sibling `isLayoutTrackingUnit` table: "The table is private to value.js—consumers receive classification, not another list to copy." Drift proof: `npx tsc --noEmit --ignoreConfig --strict --target ES2022 --moduleResolution bundler --module ESNext scratchpad/exh/probe.ts` → `tsc exit code: 0` with a 14th member added to the type and the Set literal left short.
defects.mechanism: The library owns the union as a TYPE and hides it as a VALUE, exporting no classifier. A `new Set<T>([...])` literal is checked for element assignability, never for coverage, so the consumer's hand-copy can silently fall behind the type it is annotated with. This is the root shared by L-1 (four catalogs) and L-2 (five precision rules): every consumer materialises its own copy of a fact the library declines to publish.
defects.reproduction: scratchpad/exh/probe.ts reproduces the shape with one new member added to `CssColorSpace` and the Set literal unchanged; `tsc` exits 0. The live consequence — the wrong branch of `specimenFor` — is the same reproduction as L-2/L-3.
defects.proposedCure: Do NOT export `CSS_COLOR_SPACES` — that ships the same list twice. Fold it into the library-side space registry as `SPACES[s].cssSerializable` (see L-1 cure step 1). `grammar.ts:290` reads the registry; the demo has nothing to copy; and because the registry is a mapped type over `SpaceId`, the exhaustiveness the Set literal provably lacks is enforced at the library build.

defects.defect: Display precision has five homes and no owner. `specimenFor` is a dual formatter inside one 12-line function: the CSS-serializable branch returns the library serializer's 12-digit output, the fall-through branch rounds to 4. 16 of 18 specimen rows are clipped by the CSS `truncate` clamp.
defects.evidence: `ColorSpaceSelector.vue:154-166` (the two branches; `:161` selects on CSS_PICKER_SPACES, `:163` `Number(channel.toFixed(4))`). The other homes: `src/css/grammar.ts:285` `Number(value.toFixed(12)).toString()` (what ships); `color-model.ts:67` `toCSSColorString(color, _digits = 2)` — parameter dead, verified 3/3 call sites pass no second argument; `useColorPipeline.ts:28` + `:331` `DIGITS = 2` with zero consumers; `useSliderGradients.ts:14` a second copy; `ColorComponentDisplay.vue:109` a third rule. Measured: `{"capCount":18,"truncatedCount":16,"sampleCap":{"text":"rgb(385.302835934518 143.376536829596 199.64311881105 / 82.7%)","scrollW":653,"clientW":234}}`. Adjacent DOM rows: `"HSV" → "hsv · 346.0454 · 0.6279 · 1.511"` (4 digits) vs `"HSL" → "hsl(346.045357898758deg -1295.152156124318% …)"` (12 digits). ARCHITECTURE.md: "There is no general library-string serializer" — the library deliberately declines to own this, so the demo must own it in exactly one place, and instead scattered it into five.
defects.mechanism: A single display concern (how many digits a color shows) was never given a home, so it accreted at every call site that needed it; the two live rules ended up inside one function, arbitrated by the hand-copied Set of L-16. Overflow is then handled by a Tailwind `truncate` class rather than by rounding.
defects.reproduction: `node scratchpad/repro.mjs` (18-row `[role="option"]` text dump) and scratchpad/chL-css-probe2.mjs (overflow measurement). Screenshots scratchpad/open-catalog.png and probe-catalog-open.png show `hsl(346.045357898758d…` clipped mid-token.
defects.proposedCure: One library function with one precision knob, total over all 17 spaces: `formatColor(c: AnyColor, opts?: { precision?: number }): string` exported from `@mkbabb/value.js/color` (CSS-serializable → CSS function syntax; the rest → the `space · a · b · c` form). `specimenFor` collapses to a one-line call and the CSS_PICKER_SPACES read at `:161` disappears — which is simultaneously the L-16 cure. `toCSSColorString`, both `DIGITS` constants, and `ColorComponentDisplay`'s local rule all collapse into it.

defects.defect: Out-of-gamut, non-parseable CSS ships to screen as the component's user-facing statement of "your color, in this space". The gamut decision has no home; `specimenFor` never makes one.
defects.evidence: Live DOM rows at the default `lab(92% 88.8 20 / 82.7%)`: `rgb(385.302835934518 …)` (r > 255); `hsl(346.045357898758deg -1295.152156124318% 103.662622110611% / 82.7%)` (s = −1295 %); `hwb(… 56.226092874351% -51.09915134687%)` (b < 0); `color(srgb-linear 2.580409706575 …)`. `picker-color.ts:195` already exports `clampPickerColor` and `:119` `mapPickerOklabToSrgb` wraps the library's `mapColorToGamut`; neither is on this path — `ColorSpaceSelector.vue:158-161` goes `convertPickerColor` → `serializePickerColor` with no projection step.
defects.mechanism: `serializePickerColor` (`picker-color.ts:206-211`) forwards any `CssColor` to `serializeCssColor` regardless of domain, and the component performs no projection, so the mathematically-correct-but-physically-impossible conversion is presented as valid CSS. Projection is a per-callsite choice with no owner, and this callsite never made one.
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/, click the color-space title, read any CSS-native row. Captured verbatim in the 18-row dump from `node scratchpad/repro.mjs`.
defects.proposedCure: The `formatColor` cure of L-2 takes gamut as part of its contract — project through `mapColorToGamut` before serializing, or emit the space's own valid range. One home for "how a color is shown", covering precision AND domain, since they are the same decision.

defects.defect: `demo/ui/select` is a one-line re-export barrel forwarding through the glass-ui ROOT — one of nineteen identical forwarding directories — and `docs/tranches/V/ARCHITECTURE.md:37` forbids exactly this construct by name. The component imports the same producer through a different, correct idiom eleven lines later.

ARCHITECTURE.md:37 verbatim: "There is no `panes/` dumping ground, `demo/@`, TS/Vite project alias, `@src`, or one-line glass-ui forwarding directory." Import lattice (ARCHITECTURE.md ~:50-53): `color-session → platform / shared / published packages` — `ui` is not an admitted target, and `grep -rn '"\.\./ui/' demo/color-session/` returns exactly one hit: `ColorSpaceSelector.vue:109`. glass-ui ships `./select` (74 subpath keys). The component uses the barrel at `:109` and `@mkbabb/glass-ui/watercolor-dot` at `:110`.
