Static graph: `glass-ui.js` 68 files / 225,743 B vs `select.js` 11 / 18,628 vs `watercolor-dot.js` 6 / 9,503.
defects.mechanism: A shadcn-era local-implementation layer was emptied into re-exports so call sites would not have to change — a migration shim retained for ergonomics, which is not a module boundary. It survived the W43/RF-15 boundary reform because the design law that governs it (`demo/DESIGN.md:384`) cites `@components/ui/alert`, a dead alias (`ls demo/@` → No such file or directory), and because all three eslint boundary rules match zero files (see L-5).
defects.reproduction: `grep -rn '"\.\./ui/' demo/color-session/` → one hit at ColorSpaceSelector.vue:109; read lines 102-110 of the component for the two-idiom pair. Bundle cost measured and found small — see L-17.
defects.proposedCure: Delete `demo/ui/` entirely: 19 directories, ~19 lines. Every call site imports `@mkbabb/glass-ui/<subpath>` — the idiom already dominant at 72 sites and already used by this very component for WatercolorDot. Zero new directories, zero wrappers (edict 3 satisfied by subtraction), one idiom, and ColorSpaceSelector.vue:102-110 becomes internally consistent.

defects.defect: Inverted dependency edge: `color-session` hard-injects a provider that exists only at the app composition root — and all three eslint rules written to prevent exactly this match ZERO files, so the demo's module lattice is enforced by nothing.
defects.evidence: `ColorSpaceSelector.vue:134` `const safeAccent = inject(SAFE_ACCENT_KEY)!` — no default, non-null asserted; eight lines later `:142` `inject(COLOR_MODEL_KEY, null)` — defaulted and documented. `grep -rn "provide(SAFE_ACCENT_KEY" demo/` → exactly one site: `demo/color-picker/composables/boot/useAtmosphereBoot.ts:91`, the app boot. So the runtime edge is `color-session → app boot`, the exact inversion ARCHITECTURE.md's lattice forbids. `eslint.config.js:275-286` scopes G-DEMO-1/3a/3b to `files: ["demo/@/composables/**/*.ts", "demo/@/composables/**/*.vue"]`; `ls -d demo/@` → "No such file or directory"; `find demo/@ -type f | wc -l` → 0.
defects.mechanism: The W43/RF-15 restructure moved `demo/@/composables` → `demo/color-session` and `demo/@/components` → `demo/picker` / `demo/shell` / `demo/workbenches`, but the eslint `files` globs were never repointed. The guard that would have caught this edge became a no-op, and the edge was drawn. The `!` is also a type-system lie — `inject` with no default returns `T | undefined`; on a miss `--space-title-ink` is unset, every `var(--space-title-ink)` declaration is invalid at computed-value time, and the entire W4-1 affordance grammar silently disappears without an error.
defects.reproduction: The two greps and the `ls -d demo/@` above, run and pasted. The degradation path is derived from the CSS cascade, not executed.
defects.proposedCure: Repoint the three eslint `files` globs at the real tree (`demo/color-session/**`, `demo/picker/**`, …) and ban `demo/color-picker/**` from `color-session` — it will fail immediately, which is the point. Then pass `safeAccent` as the same kind of prop `cssColor` already is (KISS, no new module), or provide `SAFE_ACCENT_KEY` from a `color-session`-owned composable that boot merely seeds.

defects.defect: The "switch color space" operation has no home. The canonical command exists in the pipeline but this component never calls it; instead each host reinvents the state write and one host's watcher performs the conversion as a side effect.
defects.evidence: `useColorPipeline.ts:170-173` defines `updateToColorSpace`. `grep -rn "updateToColorSpace" demo/` → definition, the return-object key at `:324`, and exactly one caller: `demo/picker/ColorPicker.vue:352` inside a watcher at `:348-354`. The component instead emits, and the hosts write differently: `ColorPicker.vue:43` `updateModel({ selectedColorSpace: colorSpace })` vs `AboutPane.vue:25` `model = { ...model, selectedColorSpace: colorSpace }`. AboutPane has no equivalent watcher; panes are `<KeepAlive>`d (`demo/shell/PaneSlot.vue:120`) so the picker's watcher survives a pane switch.
defects.mechanism: A command was modelled as a state mutation plus an observer, so the observer's owner (one of two hosts) became the de facto owner of the operation. The About selector works only because the Picker instance is alive to watch for it.
defects.reproduction: NONE for the break — the call-graph facts above are all verified by grep, but I did not stand up a Picker-free `/about` route, so the failure is predicted from the call graph. ARCHITECTURE.md's closed route inventory makes `/about` a first-class route and states "About is a quiet trailing destination, not Picker's permanent right-hand companion", which is when the prediction fires. LABELLED HYPOTHESIS.
defects.proposedCure: The component calls the pipeline operation directly — `commands.updateToColorSpace(space)` — and stops emitting a state write for hosts to reinvent. Both hosts lose their handler; ColorPicker loses its watcher. One command, one home, zero host-specific write mechanics.

defects.defect: God-surface injection: the component injects a 38-key composable return through a single symbol and consumes one key (2.6 % utilisation), taking a compile-time dependency on the application's entire color spine including its persistence entry points and mutators.
defects.evidence: `keys.ts:6` `COLOR_MODEL_KEY: InjectionKey<UseColorPipelineReturn>`. Counted programmatically from `useColorPipeline.ts`'s return literal: 38 keys — model, updateModel, currentPhysicalColor, cssColor, cssColorOpaque, cssColorOpaqueFrame, HSVCurrentColor, stableHue, currentColorOpaque, currentColorSpace, colorComponents, formattedCurrentColor, savedColorLabel, currentColorMeta, crownKey, canProposeName, savedColorStrings, onPaletteAddColor, onPaletteApply, parseColor, setCurrentColor, parseAndSetColor, parseAndSetColorDebounced, parseError, applyExternalColor, applyColorString, astEcho, gamutVerdict, generateRandomColor, componentsSlidersStyle, currentColorComponentsFormatted, currentColorRanges, updateToColorSpace, updateColorComponent, updateColorComponentDebounced, resetToDefaults, restoreFromStorage, DIGITS. The component uses one path: `colorModel.model.value.color` at `:156` and `:158`. `DIGITS` is in that return with zero consumers.
defects.mechanism: One composable was made the single app-wide injection symbol, so every consumer is coupled to all 38 members regardless of need. Owner edict 1 ("no god modules — focused modules with real encapsulation") is violated at the injection key, and nothing prevents a future edit inside a `<Select>` trigger from calling `restoreFromStorage` or `setCurrentColor`.
defects.reproduction: Key count produced by parsing the return literal; the two consumption sites confirmed by reading the component.
defects.proposedCure: Split `COLOR_MODEL_KEY` into role-scoped keys — `CURRENT_COLOR_KEY` (`ComputedRef<PickerColor>`), `COLOR_COMMANDS_KEY` (the mutation surface), `COLOR_NAMING_KEY`. This component injects `CURRENT_COLOR_KEY` plus `COLOR_COMMANDS_KEY` (for L-6) and nothing else. No new directory and no wrapper component — three symbols in the file that already holds five.

defects.defect: The `demo/ui/` barrel's bundle cost — left unmeasured by the first pass — is 1,044 bytes (7.8 %), not the 12× the raw static graph suggests. Reported to prevent an overstated claim; L-4 stands on structure alone.
defects.evidence: `npx esbuild via-barrel.js --bundle --minify --format=esm --external:vue --external:reka-ui --external:@lucide/vue --external:@mkbabb/keyframes.js --external:@mkbabb/value.js/{color,css}` → 14,441 bytes; the identical entry importing `@mkbabb/glass-ui/select` → 13,397 bytes. glass-ui declares `"sideEffects": ["*.css"]`, so the shake is legitimate. The unshaken static graph is 68 files / 225,743 B (root) vs 11 / 18,628 (select) vs 6 / 9,503 (watercolor-dot). The production artifact could not corroborate: `dist/gh-pages/assets` contains 2 JS files totalling 16 KB for the whole application.
defects.mechanism: Raw reachable-graph size overstates cost for a side-effect-free ES module package; measuring the shaken output is the only honest number. Recording it converts L-4 from a size argument (weak) into a pure structure argument (strong and sufficient).
defects.reproduction: The two esbuild invocations above, run and byte-counted; graph census by transitive `./`-relative closure over `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist`.
defects.proposedCure: No cure needed for the bytes. Keep the L-4 cure (delete `demo/ui/`) and justify it on the three-parallel-idioms census (48 / 37 / 72) rather than on weight; do not let a future reader defeat L-4 by disproving a size claim that was never load-bearing.

defects.defect: `tsconfig.demo.json`'s `paths` block for `@mkbabb/value.js` is redundant where it is right and dead where it is wrong: three entries point at files that do not exist, two published subpaths are omitted, and the header advertises a "CLOSED 8-key set" that does not match the exports map — a documented false statement of the public surface.
defects.evidence: `package.json#exports` = `./color ./value ./css ./easing ./math ./transform ./quantize` (7 keys, no `.`). `tsconfig.demo.json:42-49` lists the bare root → `./dist/index.d.ts`, `/parsing`, `/units` — all three targets verified ABSENT — and omits `/css` and `/value`. Yet `npx tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit --traceResolution` shows `@mkbabb/value.js/css` (which has no `paths` entry) resolving correctly via `Found 'package.json' … Entering conditional exports … Using 'exports' subpath './css' with target './dist/subpaths/css.d.ts'`. Latent trap: the Vite alias set is generated from `Object.entries(exports)` (`vite.config.ts:34-51`), which has no `.` key, so a bare `@mkbabb/value.js` specifier is unaliased and would resolve to `node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js` — a real self-install of the published 4.0.0 tarball whose `css.d.ts` AND `css.js` differ from the local `dist/` (`diff -rq` → 2 files differ).
defects.mechanism: The Vite alias side is generated from the exports map and cannot drift; the TS side is hand-maintained and did. The block survives because self-package `exports` resolution silently covers every gap it leaves, so nothing ever fails.
defects.reproduction: `for f in dist/index.d.ts dist/subpaths/parsing.d.ts dist/subpaths/units.d.ts; do [ -e "$f" ] || echo MISSING $f; done` → all three MISSING. The traceResolution excerpt above. For the trap: `grep -rn 'from "@mkbabb/value\.js"' demo/ src/` and the same over both installed siblings' `dist/` → ZERO bare-root importers today, so the trap is a HYPOTHESIS: mechanism verified, triggering import does not yet exist.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the `@mkbabb/value.js*` `paths` entries outright rather than fixing them. Self-name resolution through the real `exports` map cannot drift from the map by construction — the same argument `vite.config.ts` already makes for generating the Vite aliases. Applying that logic to the TS side means subtraction, not a second generator. Optionally add a `"."` key to `exports` (or an explicit alias) so the bare specifier can never silently reach the stale self-install.

defects.defect: `color-model.ts` is three-sixths shim: a zero-consumer rename alias, a delegation with a dead parameter, and a second delegation the subject component imports alongside the very module it wraps — the dual path visible in eleven lines.
defects.evidence: `color-model.ts:58` `export const CSS_NATIVE_SPACES = CSS_PICKER_SPACES` — `grep -rn "CSS_NATIVE_SPACES" demo/ src/ | wc -l` → 1, its own definition. `:61` `colorToHexString` is `return pickerColorToHex(color)`. `:67` `toCSSColorString(color, _digits: number = 2)` returns `serializePickerColor(color)`; all three call sites (`ColorPicker.vue:293`, `useColorPipeline.ts:214`, `:216`) pass no second argument. `ColorSpaceSelector.vue:117-122` imports `colorToHexString` from `color-model` while `:112-116` imports `convertPickerColor`, `serializePickerColor` and `CSS_PICKER_SPACES` from `picker-color` — the wrapper and the wrapped module in one import block.
defects.mechanism: Renames retained after a refactor so call sites would not change (owner edict 2, "no aliases, migration shims, dual paths"), plus a signature frozen after its parameter was abandoned.
defects.reproduction: The three greps above, run and counted.
defects.proposedCure: `color-model.ts` dissolves. `DISPLAY_COLOR_SPACE_NAMES` and `resolveColorSpace` → the space catalog (L-1 cure); `EditTarget` → `keys.ts`, whose `EDIT_TARGET_KEY` is its only structural neighbour; the three aliases delete and their call sites import `pickerColorToHex` / `serializePickerColor` directly.

defects.defect: Two v-model idioms in one 45-line script, and the hand-rolled half widens `DisplayColorSpace` to `string` on the component's public surface, manufacturing four cast sites.
defects.evidence: `ColorSpaceSelector.vue:125` `modelValue: string` in the props block + `:146-148` `defineEmits<{ "update:modelValue": [value: string] }>` (pre-3.4 pair), beside `:144` `defineModel<boolean>("open", …)` (3.4+). defects.reproduction: Read the four cited lines; grep confirms all three host-side `any` sites. defects.defect: The mega-tranche visual harness cannot see any defect in this report: it covers 15 routes but captures each once in its default state, and the production build it would otherwise corroborate against emits 16 KB of JS for the entire application.

result.strongestDefect: D-3 — The specimen catalog, the component's entire reason to exist, fails on legibility, completeness and truth simultaneously: the numeric headline bleeds through the glass panel and interleaves with the first option's caption (D-open-1440-dark.png, D-open-390-light.png where the first row's NAME is clipped off entirely); 16 of 18 captions truncate (worst case 234px available / 741px needed = 32% shown, so the "live per-space conversion" the component promises at ColorSpaceSelector.vue:56-57 is never delivered); the strings themselves are unclamped nonsense at 15 significant digits (`rgb(385.302835934518 ...)` — R=385 on a 0-255 axis; `hsl(... -1295.152156124318% 103.662622110611% ...)`) and self-contradictory (the same colour's red channel reads 385 in the RGB row and 255 in the `#ff8fc8d3` hex row three rows later); and only 4 of 18 rows (22%) are visible at once, 3 of 18 at the 720px zoom arm. defects.defect: In forced-colors mode the trigger has ZERO state delta: rest, hover and focus render byte-identically. `outline: none` deletes the UA fallback and `box-shadow` is the sole focus indicator, but box-shadow computes to `none` under forced-color-adjust:auto (CSS Color Adjust L1 §3.2); separately the rest-state `text-decoration-color: transparent` is painted as CanvasText in forced colors, consuming the hover delta before hover fires.

The identical clip in the normal path registers 5.21% / 5.48% / 10.69%, so the clip is correct and the zero is real. Computed styles agree: forced-colors `triggerBoxShadow:"none"`, `triggerOutlineStyle:"none"`, `triggerColor:"rgb(255,255,255)"` at rest AND focus. Frame: D-focus-forcedcolors.png. Law: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:84 "Focus remains visibly distinct from selection in both schemes, forced colors and reduced transparency"; :90 "focus has its own independent nonzero delta".
defects.mechanism: F1 — local register instead of producer register: the component mints its own focus ring in a scoped block instead of consuming glass-ui's SelectTrigger focus register
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/ColorSpaceSelector/probe-D3.mjs (dev server live on 127.0.0.1:9000) — prints the three state deltas for forced-colors and normal; artifacts D-state-fc-{rest,hover,focus}.png are byte-identical.

If glass-ui 7.0.0's SelectTrigger focus register is itself box-shadow-only, the fix is an `outline`-based focus primitive IN glass-ui (edict 4) relayed to the BH inbox — not a second consumer override. An outline survives forced colors by spec; a box-shadow cannot.

defects.defect: The P019 paired-clamp law is not implemented. The identity and the headline scale on two different bases — a `vw` clamp vs a `cqi` expression times a runtime JS factor — so a fixed ratio is structurally impossible. Measured ratio drifts 0.729 → 0.975 and is 0.975 at the desktop reference viewport, a +24.0% error against the required 1/√φ.
defects.evidence: Identity: ColorSpaceSelector.vue:209 `font-size: var(--type-display-2)` = clamp(2.058rem, 1.5rem + 2.2vw, 3.33rem) — viewport-driven. Headline: demo/picker/display/ColorComponentDisplay/ColorComponentDisplay.vue:136-139 `font-size: calc(min(var(--type-display-4), max(11.65cqi, 2.618rem)) * var(--readout-fit, 1))` — container-driven times a JS factor. Measured (probe-D.mjs; 1/√φ = 0.786151): 1440x900 → 53.280/54.646 = 0.9750 (+24.0%); 720x450 → 39.840/54.646 = 0.7290 (-7.3%); 390x844 → 32.928/41.888 = 0.7861 (exact); 320x700 → 0.7861 (exact). The law holds at the floor arm only, because 2.058rem/2.618rem happens to equal 1/√φ. Confirmed stable across five colour spaces at 1440: Lab, OKLCh, ProPhoto RGB, Hex, Kelvin all report ratio=0.9750 err=24.0%. Law: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:62 "BI P019 supplies a paired clamp whose complete rendered ratio is 1/√φ; independently clamped display-2/display-3 tokens and a local approximation are forbidden"; PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:46 (PR-02) "`Lab` competes typographically with numeric specimen → TIGHTEN". Visual confirmation: ../../visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/picker.png — "Lab" and "92.0%, 88.8, 20.0" read as the same optical weight, and the Fraunces italic is heavier in colour than the Fira numerals so optically the label wins.
defects.mechanism: F2 — two scaling bases: identity on vw, headline on cqi times a JS factor
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/ColorSpaceSelector/probe-D.mjs — compare `triggers[].fontSize` against `headlineCandidates[0].fs` per arm. PR-02's TIGHTEN was never delivered; only the T-51 one-rung step-down (:200-208) landed, and it moved the wrong arm.
defects.proposedCure: One clamp, one base. Either both arms consume `cqi` from the same container, or the producer ships the P019 paired token and both arms consume it. Two independent clamps cannot be patched into agreement — the ratio must resolve from a single source through floor, fluid arm and ceiling, exactly as §3.2 specifies.

defects.defect: The focus ring measures 1.76–2.09 : 1 against its own plate in every arm, below the WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 non-text-contrast floor of 3.00 : 1 — and its contrast is a free variable of the user's picked colour, not a design decision. The ring is also optically unbalanced around the word it encircles.
defects.evidence: Measured (probe-D4.mjs; ring = median of the 500 largest-delta pixels between rest and focus screenshots, ground = the same pixels at rest, WCAG relative luminance): dark-default ring=[168 130 151] plate=[122 74 105] → 2.09:1; light-default ring=[217 118 164] plate=[244 181 217] → 1.76:1; light-default-about ring=[218 139 163] plate=[246 214 215] → 1.89:1. Root: `--focus-ring-shadow` = `0 0 0 2px color-mix(in srgb, <accent> 30%, transparent), 0 0 8px color-mix(…, 15%, transparent)` (probe-D2.mjs output) — a 30%-alpha ring cannot reach 3:1 against a mid-lightness ground by construction; and demo/styles/foundation.css:263 re-points `--focus-ring-color` at `--accent-live`, the live picked colour. Optical balance: D-focus-normal.png shows an 111.5x85 rounded rect around ~53px of ink with ~25px headroom above the cap and ~10px below the descender — asymmetric by construction because `h-fit` measures the line box and ColorSpaceSelector.vue:224 adds `padding: 0 0 0.095em` on the bottom only. Laws: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:82 "Text, focus, boundaries and state meet their rendered contrast on the actual material tier; a token name is not evidence"; PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:56 (PR-12) and :72 "Visual glyph size, operable target size and layout reservation are separate quantities". The component's comment at :273-275 asserts "the ring must stay visible" — unverified, and false in the forced-colors mode (D-1).
defects.mechanism: F1 — local register instead of producer register
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/ColorSpaceSelector/probe-D4.mjs, then the PIL contrast computation over D-ring-*-{rest,focus}.png pairs (pasted in the report §D-5).
defects.proposedCure: Same cure as D-1 — delete the local focus block and let glass-ui own focus at the root. The producer ring must be an `outline` at an alpha that can clear 3:1 on the resting-plate tier in both schemes; if `--focus-ring-color` is to keep riding `--accent-live`, its certification must include the ring-vs-plate ratio, not only the ink-vs-plate ratio.

defects.defect: Selecting a colour space through this component reflows the picker chassis by 61.2px, shoving the spectrum canvas and every slider below it. The readout also reserves a blank first line for two of the spaces.
defects.evidence: Measured (WebKit 1440x900, driving the component's own dropdown; script and output in the report appendix): `{"s":"Lab","headerH":226.5,"lines":"2"}` `{"s":"OKLCh","headerH":226.5,"lines":"2"}` `{"s":"ProPhoto RGB","headerH":165.3,"lines":"1"}` `{"s":"Hex","headerH":165.3,"lines":"1"}` `{"s":"Kelvin","headerH":165.3,"lines":"1"}` — header height 226.5 → 165.3px, a 61.2px jump. Blank reservation: at 1440 the readout <h3> box top y=252.6 while the first `.readout-cell` ink top is y=313.8 — 61.2px of reserved emptiness above a single-line value, i.e. PR-01's "unconditional two-line/bottom-aligned readout" (PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:11,45) is still shipping at HEAD. Visible in ../../visual/shots/zoom-200-desktop/picker.png as an enormous unowned void between "Lab" and the numerals. Laws: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:78 "Live numbers … reserve their widest legal representation so value changes never reflow the settled chassis"; :30 "Expanded/collapsed/mounted states do not move the scene below it"; :98 "Selection changes the active specimen without committing it"; PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:19 "The locked chassis does not grow for paint or values".
defects.mechanism: F2 — two scaling bases; the reservation is driven by a per-space line count that the identity arm does not share
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/ at 1440x900, select Lab, then select Hex — the spectrum canvas jumps 61.2px up. Scripted in the report appendix (p6-style: select each space, read `.picker-header` and `.readout` rects).
defects.proposedCure: Mechanism owner is readoutReservation.ts / W20, not this file — but this component is the sole trigger and must be part of the fix. Reserve the widest legal representation once (VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:78) so `--readout-lines` never changes with the selected space, and drop the bottom-aligned two-line minimum entirely per PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:19 clause 5.

defects.defect: Two comboboxes with the identical accessible name "Select color space" render on one route, driving one piece of state. The root cause is compositional: About ships as Picker's companion pane instead of the `/about` member route the constitution declares, so the component instantiates twice on the same screen.
defects.evidence: Measured (probe-D.mjs, every desktop arm): `triggerCount: 2`; both `role="combobox"`, both `aria-label="Select color space"` (ColorSpaceSelector.vue:43), both bound to `model.selectedColorSpace`. Hosts: demo/picker/ColorPicker.vue:39 (plate title, 53.28px) and demo/scenes/about/AboutPane.vue:20 (inline, 41.89px). Visible in ../../visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/picker.png — "Lab" top-left AND "About the color spaces, *Lab*" top-right, both operable. Route table: demo/color-picker/router/index.ts:22-37 has NO `/about` route. Laws: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:50 (PR-06) "Three adjacent action species or duplicated selected fills → REMOVE. One action/selection owner"; VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:58 "About is a quiet trailing destination rather than Picker's companion" and the member-route inventory names `/about`; :44 abrogates the companion composition. Consequence for the audit: the `inline` host has zero coverage in the tracked visual matrix — the 15 captured routes (../../visual/REPORT.md:119-178) contain no `/#/about`, so no matrix arm exercises the inline branch on its own terms.
defects.mechanism: F4 — compositional duplication: the companion-pane composition the constitution abrogates
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/ColorSpaceSelector/probe-D.mjs — every 1440 arm reports triggerCount 2 with identical ariaLabel. Or: open http://localhost:9000/#/ at 1440 and count the operable "Lab" controls.
defects.proposedCure: Land `/about` as a real route (W18 owns About's body, W19 owns route/Dock/title reachability per VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:58). The second combobox disappears with the companion pane — this is not fixed by renaming one of the two aria-labels, which would leave two selection owners for one state.

defects.defect: Six consumer overrides defeat glass-ui internals, three of them self-labelled "BOOKED SWAP" pending a producer cure; one of those cures has already landed in the installed glass-ui 7.0.0 and the patch — plus its now-false written justification — did not retire. The component also passes a producer `size` prop and then overrides font-size outright.
defects.evidence: Overrides: (1) ColorSpaceSelector.vue:48 `[&>span]:overflow-visible [&>span]:line-clamp-none [&>span]:block [&_svg]:translate-y-[0.06em]` defeats SelectTrigger label/svg layout; (2) :224 `padding: 0 0 0.095em` defeats the producer's `px-3 py-2` (self-documented at :219-223); (3) :239-242 `.space-trigger :deep(svg){width/height:0.382em}` defeats the chevron's h-4/w-4; (4) :249-255 `.space-trigger > :deep(span)` decorates reka's cloned SelectValue node; (5) :65 `class="pl-3 pr-4 py-2"` defeats SelectItem padding; (6) :300-302 `.specimen-name{font-weight:var(--type-weight-display)}` defeats text-title's weight. STALE RATIONALE: :291-299 states "glass-ui's `text-title` @utility hardcodes `font-weight: 700` (semantic.css:132) — a UTILITY hardcode, not a token". At the installed glass-ui 7.0.0, `grep -o 'text-title { [^}]*}' node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/typography/semantic.css` returns `font-weight: var(--type-weight-title)` — a token (`--type-weight-title: 700`), not a hardcode. The producer cure landed; the consumer patch did not retire. Also :45 passes `size="default"` and :209 then overrides font-size. Owner edicts 4 (glass-ui is the design system), 5 (root-level styling, never per-instance overrides), 2 (no legacy code, no dual paths).
defects.mechanism: F1/F5 — local register instead of producer register, compounded by stale self-documentation whose precondition has been met
defects.reproduction: grep -o 'text-title { [^}]*}' node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/typography/semantic.css — the utility now reads `font-weight: var(--type-weight-title)`, contradicting the comment at ColorSpaceSelector.vue:293-295.
defects.proposedCure: Audit every "BOOKED SWAP" comment as a debt with a checkable precondition, retire the ones now due, and delete the prose that is no longer true. For the weight pin specifically the root-level cure is available: re-point `--type-weight-title` at the demo :root, or better, stop using a *title* utility for a dropdown option at all (see D-9). Every remaining need moves into a glass-ui variant and is relayed to the active BH inbox (edicts 4 + 5), not patched a second time in the consumer.

defects.defect: The dropdown option name renders at 2.01x the legislated size in the wrong font family, against a type matrix the constitution declares closed. The class list also stacks two conflicting family utilities and relies on cascade order to pick a winner.
defects.evidence: ColorSpaceSelector.vue:76-78 `class="specimen-name font-display italic text-title leading-tight"`. Measured (probe-D.mjs, every open arm): `nameFontSize: 32.928001px`, `nameFamily: "Fraunces"`, `nameWeight: 400`. Tokens from source: `--type-title: 2.058rem` = 32.928px; `--type-small: clamp(0.875rem, 0.8rem + 0.25vw, 1.25rem)` = 16.4px at 1440. 32.928/16.4 = 2.01x, in the display family, italic. Laws: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:75 "control or label, including dropdown options → `text-small` | Plus Jakarta Sans, non-bold"; :78 "This matrix is closed across all eighteen compositions"; PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:15 "Dropdown options remain Plus Jakarta Sans `text-small` control copy and non-bold". Family conflict: `text-title` itself sets `font-family: var(--font-text)` while the same class list also carries `font-display`; the measured winner is Fraunces, decided by utility cascade order rather than by declaration. Rendered consequence (crop-dark, D-open-390-light.png): a stack of headlines rather than a control list — which is the direct cause of only 4 of 18 rows fitting (D-3e).
defects.mechanism: F3 — the catalog was designed as typography, not as a control
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/ColorSpaceSelector/probe-D.mjs — every open arm prints `nameFS=32.928001px nameFam=Fraunces`.
defects.proposedCure: Drop `font-display italic text-title` and take the legislated `text-small` control rung in Plus Jakarta Sans, non-bold. That single change removes the family conflict, removes the need for the weight pin at :300-302 (D-8), roughly halves the row height, and lets 18 rows read as one catalog instead of four headlines.

defects.defect: The host sheet reaches into the component and replaces its declared transition with a `font-size` animation — a property that forces layout on every frame for 300ms. The header comment misstates this as a single bounded reflow.
defects.evidence: demo/picker/header.css:95-102: `.picker-header .space-trigger { transition: color var(--duration-fast) …, font-size var(--duration-normal) …; }` plus `.picker-header.is-condensed .space-trigger { font-size: var(--type-display-1); }`. Measured (probe-D.mjs): the picker instance reports `transition: "color, font-size / 0.2s, 0.3s"` while the About instance reports `"color / 0.2s"` — the component's own ColorSpaceSelector.vue:192 `transition: color var(--duration-fast) var(--ease-standard)` is silently clobbered, `.picker-header .space-trigger` (0,2,0) beating `.space-trigger` (0,1,0), both unlayered. header.css:31-33 claims "Bounded 300ms reflow at the crossing, ZERO per-frame reflow during scroll" — the second clause holds, the first does not: a font-size transition reflows the header band and everything below it in the scrolling Card on every frame of the 300ms (~18 full layout passes at 60fps).
defects.mechanism: F2 — two scaling bases, and edict 5 inverted: the host per-instance-overrides the component instead of the component styling at the root
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/ColorSpaceSelector/probe-D.mjs — compare `triggers[0].transition` (picker, "color, font-size / 0.2s, 0.3s") with `triggers[1].transition` (About inline, "color / 0.2s").
defects.proposedCure: Make the condense a discrete rung swap with no transition on font-size — exactly what the readout in the same sheet already does and documents at header.css:109-115 ("the readout SNAPS on condense … animating them would both violate the lock and be caught mid-transition"). If a smooth condensed title is genuinely wanted, it belongs as a producer-owned condensed size station on SelectTrigger, not as a host sheet reaching into a child component's class.

defects.defect: The component's documented reduced-motion behaviour is false. The global guard does not neutralise its transitions; a carve-out written for overlay primitives replaces them with an opacity transition the component never authored.
defects.evidence: ColorSpaceSelector.vue:186-188 claims "the global PRM guard (animations.css) neutralises these transition durations; states still land instantly as ink." Measured under `reducedMotion: "reduce"` (probe-D.mjs, arm wk-1440-prm): `transition: "opacity / 0.15s"` — not neutralised, replaced. Source: demo/styles/animations.css:202-212 carves out `[data-state="open"], [data-state="closed"]` with `transition-property: opacity !important; transition-duration: 150ms !important`, and the SelectTrigger carries `data-state="closed"` at rest. demo/picker/header.css:136-143's own PRM guard sets duration only and is therefore dead. The component has no PRM contract of its own; whichever global sheet sorts last wins.
defects.mechanism: F5 — stale self-documentation: the scoped prose describes a cascade that no longer exists
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/ColorSpaceSelector/probe-D.mjs — arm `wk-1440-prm` prints `transition: "opacity / 0.15s"` on both trigger instances.
defects.proposedCure: Narrow the animations.css:202-212 carve-out to the overlay primitives it was written for (Dialog/Sheet/Popover content roots), not every `[data-state]` element in the app; then delete the now-redundant duration-only guard at header.css:136-143 and correct the component comment at :186-188.

defects.defect: Eleven hand-minted literals in a component whose stated thesis is that the glass-ui token ladder is the sizing authority. Each is justified in prose as "the exact optical ratio at the display-1 basis" — a basis the component itself abandoned at :209.
defects.evidence: ColorSpaceSelector.vue:191 `86%` · :216 `gap: 0.19em` · :224 `padding: 0 0 0.095em` · :240-241 `width/height: 0.382em` (x2) · :251-252 `0.024em` and `0.072em` · :283-284 `0.875rem` (x2) · :288 `opacity: 0.35` · :48 `translate-y-[0.06em]` · :80 `max-w-[16rem]`. None is a token. The component's own comment at :193-199 declares "the glass-ui ladder is the sizing AUTHORITY" while :236-238 mints 0.382em as "today's exact optical ratio (1rem at the 41.89px display-1 cap)" — a frozen guess about a basis that :200-208 stepped away from. PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:73 "Real rendered relation wins over token intent" cuts both ways: a hand-derived em ratio is neither a token nor a measured relation.
defects.mechanism: F5 — stale self-documentation and locally minted scale
defects.reproduction: NONE — this is a source-level enumeration, verifiable by reading ColorSpaceSelector.vue:190-310.
defects.proposedCure: Each literal is either (a) a producer concern — caret size, control padding, item padding — in which case it moves into a glass-ui variant, or (b) a genuine demo token, in which case it is named in demo/styles and consumed. Nothing in this component needs a bare number: the caret ratio, the underline pair and the dot diameter are all design-system quantities.

defects.defect: Two model idioms in one component; a `required` two-way model whose only real consumer is a hidden Cmd+K keybinding, leaving one host with a write-only ref; `any` casts in the template masking a type mismatch; and colour-space conversion plus two number-formatting grammars living inside a selector component.
defects.evidence: ColorSpaceSelector.vue:125 + :146-148 use the legacy prop + defineEmits pair for `modelValue`, while :144 uses `defineModel` for `open` — two idioms in one file (owner edict 7, idiomatic Vue 3.5; `defineModel<string>()` replaces the pair). `defineModel<boolean>("open", { required: true })` forces every host to own an open ref: demo/scenes/about/AboutPane.vue:73 `const aboutSelectOpen = ref(false)` is declared, bound at :22, and never read — write-only. The only real consumer is demo/picker/ColorPicker.vue:265 `selectedColorSpaceOpen.value = !selectedColorSpaceOpen.value` under a `Cmd+K` handler — an unlabelled, undiscoverable keyboard affordance (PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:51, PR-07 "Hover-only/unlabeled controls"). `any` casts: ColorSpaceSelector.vue:11 `(colorSpace: any)`, repeated at ColorPicker.vue:43 and AboutPane.vue:25; the emit is typed `[value: string]` and the `any` masks the reka `AcceptableValue` mismatch rather than resolving it (edict 2, no masking fallbacks). Cohesion: `specimenFor` (:154-166) performs conversion, serialization and two incompatible number formats inside a selector component.
defects.mechanism: F5 — API and idiom drift accumulated across waves without a consolidating pass
defects.reproduction: grep -rn 'selectedColorSpaceOpen\|aboutSelectOpen' demo/ — aboutSelectOpen appears exactly twice (declaration at AboutPane.vue:73, binding at :22) and is never read.
defects.proposedCure: Collapse to one idiom: `const modelValue = defineModel<DisplayColorSpace>()` and `const open = defineModel<boolean>('open')` without `required`, which types the emit correctly and deletes all three `any` casts at once. Move `specimenFor`'s formatting beside `serializePickerColor` so the catalog and the readout share one canonical grammar (which also cures D-3d). Give the Cmd+K affordance a visible name or delete it.

defects.defect: Physical `padding-left`/`padding-right` on the option row in a document that declares a direction, and no bidi isolation on captions that are CSS strings full of paired brackets. The asymmetric 12/16px gutter is additionally vestigial — it was tuned for the indicator-less row.
defects.evidence: ColorSpaceSelector.vue:65 `class="pl-3 pr-4 py-2"` — physical, measured `paddingLeft: 12px / paddingRight: 16px`. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:150 "chrome, navigation and layout | logical inline/block direction follows the document"; the logical form `ps-3 pe-4` is the same character count. The `.specimen-caption` carries no `dir="ltr"`, no `<bdi>`, computed `unicodeBidi: "normal"` and `dir` attribute null; VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:154 "CSS strings, hex, slugs, IDs and provenance | render in LTR-isolated spans inside RTL prose". Captions such as `lab(92% 88.8 20 / 82.7%)` contain paired brackets, which UAX #9 rule BD16 mirrors in an RTL paragraph. The 12px leading gutter is also too small to clear the producer indicator's `left-2 + w-3.5` = 22px if D-2 is cured.
defects.mechanism: F1/F3 — physical rather than logical box properties, and an un-isolated domain string in a prose container
defects.reproduction: HYPOTHESIS for the rendered mirroring only. With `document.documentElement.dir = "rtl"` the app still computes `direction: ltr` on both the trigger and the caption (probe measured `triggerDir: "ltr"`, `capDir: "ltr"`, `capUnicodeBidi: "normal"`, `capDirAttr: null`), so RTL is presently pinned off and the mirroring cannot be exhibited live. The code-level absence of logical properties and of bidi isolation is FACT, verifiable at ColorSpaceSelector.vue:65 and :87-92.
defects.proposedCure: Use logical `ps-*`/`pe-*` and size the leading gutter from the producer indicator's geometry rather than a tuned constant. Wrap the caption value in `<bdi>` (or `dir="ltr"` + `unicode-bidi: isolate`), which is what VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:154 already requires for every CSS string, hex, slug and ID in the app — this is a house-wide rule, so the cure belongs in whatever shared value-rendering primitive the demo has, not in this file alone.

defects.defect: In dark mode the component's one chromatic gesture is achromatic: the certified accent loses 89% of its chroma, so the title that carries the product's colour identity in light mode paints near-white in dark. The component compounds it by hard-coding an 86% alpha with no reference to the tier it lands on, yielding two different rendered contrasts for one "grammar".
defects.evidence: Measured `--accent-live` (probe-D4.mjs): light `oklch(47.118925176164% 0.188447570516 9.83402284231deg)` chroma 0.188; dark `oklch(95.832172477266% 0.021053120065 9.83402284231deg)` chroma 0.021 — a 89% chroma loss. Rendered trigger ink (probe-D.mjs): light `color(srgb 0.665034 0 0.261497 / 0.86)` — saturated crimson; dark `color(srgb 1 0.924654 0.933001 / 0.86)` — effectively white. Visible in ../../visual/shots/safari-desktop-dark/picker.png. Two rendered contrasts for one ink: PIL sampling of the tracked Safari light capture (peak ink pixel vs modal background over the title bounding box) gives 3.89:1 on the picker plate (bg 236,185,212 / ink 179,26,87) and 4.79:1 on the About plate (bg 247,216,216 / ink 181,30,88) — a 23% spread, because ColorSpaceSelector.vue:191 fixes `color-mix(in srgb, var(--space-title-ink) 86%, transparent)` without reference to the tier. Laws: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:21 sanctions seed tint for the "active accent"; :144 "No path desaturates through gray"; :82 "a token name is not evidence".
defects.mechanism: F3 — the chromatic identity is delegated to a certifier that optimises luminance contrast alone, then a fixed alpha is applied on top without re-certifying against the actual tier
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/ColorSpaceSelector/probe-D4.mjs prints `accentLive` per scheme; the two-host contrast spread is reproduced by the PIL block pasted in report §D-15 over the tracked Safari captures.
defects.proposedCure: Mechanism owner is `certifyAccentInk` / demo/color-session/useContrastSafeColor.ts:302-311, not this file — the certifier must preserve a chroma floor in dark, not only a luminance ratio, or the "active accent" ceases to be one. In this component, delete the 86% alpha and let the certified ink be the rest ink, deriving hover from a second certified rung: an alpha applied after certification silently un-certifies the result and makes the rendered contrast host-dependent.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/color-session/ColorSpaceSelector.vue (area core, ~311 lines)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`, read from this seat's own system prompt ("You are powered by the model named Opus 5 (1M context). The exact model ID is claude-opus-5[1m]"), matching the explicit declaration this seat was spawned with. Not inherited, not undeclared.
result.strongestDefect: C-1 — `specimenFor()` (ColorSpaceSelector.vue:154-166) calls the throwing `convertPickerColor` inside a render expression for all 18 catalog rows, with no guard. Pure white (`rgb(255 255 255)`) fails RGB→HSL with `color_non_finite`, the throw escapes render, and `ErrorBoundary` (App.vue:50) replaces the ENTIRE picker pane with a blank grey field. Reachable by a plain user gesture — press `End` on the R slider then `End` on the G slider in RGB space — and the dropdown is never even opened, because reka teleports closed SelectContent into a DocumentFragment (SelectContent.js:158-161) so all 18 rows render at rest.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (Recorded anyway, since absence of findings in these areas is evidence: word-boundary grep for addEventListener|requestAnimationFrame|setTimeout|setInterval|onMounted|onUnmounted|onBeforeUnmount|watch|watchEffect|ResizeObserver|IntersectionObserver over the file returns 0 hits (exit 1) — no leak/cleanup/PRM-RAF class exists here. Keyboard is fully operable (Enter opens 18 options, ArrowDown highlights, typeahead "oklch" lands on OKLCh, Enter selects, focus returns to the trigger; Escape closes and restores focus). Tap targets: picker trigger 111.5x85, About trigger 88.6x48, option rows 284x80.7 — all >=24px, so 0 contribution to the visual REPORT's 60 smallTapTargets; the trigger is a named <button>, 0 contribution to the 18 namelessButtons. verbatimModuleSyntax compliant (line 122 is the only type-only import and uses `import type`). Vue 3.5 reactive props destructure used correctly; `openModel` is never read after being written, so the defineModel stale-read hazard does not bite — verified live by rapid XYZ→Kelvin→Hex selection from the About host with both instances staying in sync. No animations deleted, no legacy shims, not a god module.)

defects.defect: `specimenFor()` calls the throwing `convertPickerColor`/`serializePickerColor`/`colorToHexString` APIs unguarded inside a render expression, once per catalog row for all 18 rows. A reachable colour (pure white) makes the conversion throw during render, and the escaped throw destroys the entire picker pane via ErrorBoundary — leaving the user on a blank grey screen with a single 'Try again' pill.
defects.evidence:
demo/color-session/ColorSpaceSelector.vue:154-166 (specimenFor), :91 (call site inside the v-for at :61); demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:104-107 (`valueOrThrow` = unconditional throw), :115-117 (`convertPickerColor`). LIVE STACK captured by patching globalThis.Error before module eval:
```
color_non_finite
Error: color_non_finite
    at valueOrThrow (demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:154:8)
    at convertPickerColor (demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:162:9)
    at Proxy.specimenFor (demo/color-session/ColorSpaceSelector.vue:50:22)
    at demo/color-session/ColorSpaceSelector.vue:144:35
    at renderFnWithContext (vue.runtime.esm-bundler)
```
(compiled Vite offsets; sources are picker-color.ts:106/:116 and ColorSpaceSelector.vue:157). Library-level mechanism, no browser: `convertColor(rgb(255 255 255), 'hsl')` -> `THROWCODE color_non_finite` while `rgb(254 255 255)` -> `[180.0000000000034, 0.9999999999999434, 0.9980392156862745]` (RGB→HSL divides by `2-max-min == 0` only at exact white). Screenshots: evidence/C1-white-rgb-dead.png, evidence/C1-white-hex-dead.png, evidence/C-live-slider-to-white.png.
defects.mechanism: Fallible domain API (Result-returning `convertColor` wrapped into a throwing `valueOrThrow`) invoked from a template expression with no guard. The sibling code in the same domain treats the identical call as fallible (useColorPipeline.ts:88-95 wraps `convertPickerColor(m.color,'hsv')` in try/catch); this component is the only surface converting the live colour into EVERY space and the only one with no guard.
defects.reproduction:
A (pure gesture, no deep link, dropdown never opened): boot `http://localhost:9000/#/?space=rgb&color=rgb(253 254 255)`, focus the R slider, press `End`, focus the G slider, press `End`. Measured output:
```
booted, triggers: 2  boundary: 0
   after slider 0 -> boundary: 0
   after slider 1 -> boundary: 1        <- pane DEAD
   slider 2 gone (pane already dead)
URL: http://localhost:9000/#/?space=rgb&color=rgb(255+255+255)
non_finite errors captured: 1
```

defects.evidence:

Write path: useColorPipeline.ts:64-71 `updateModel` applies `clampColorToSpaceDomain(patch.color)` (the T-33a 'ONE write gate'), reached via `updateToColorSpace` -> `setCurrentColor` (useColorPipeline.ts:170-173). PROMISE HSL: hsl(346.045357898758deg -1295.152156124318% 103.662622110611% / 82.7%)

XYZ promised color(xyz 1.266749228777 …) ; delivered color(xyz 1 …)

defects.mechanism: Two code paths compute the same quantity with different laws — the preview reads the raw conversion, the commit reads the clamped conversion. This makes the preview definitionally equal to the result, and simultaneously kills the invalid-CSS output, because clamping is what turns `-1295%` into `0%`.

The false premise has been propagated to three sibling components as 'the ColorSpaceSelector precedent'.
defects.evidence:

Propagation: demo/workbenches/mix/MixConfigBar.vue:21 ('reka unmounts it closed — the ColorSpaceSelector precedent'), demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue:91 ('the ColorSpaceSelector precedent), so zero rest cost'), demo/shell/dock/DockViewSelect.vue:102.

Object.fromEntries(spaceEntries.map(([s]) => [s, formatSpecimen(s)])) : EMPTY)`. One derivation per colour change instead of 36 per render pass per instance; nothing computed while closed; and because the gate is `openModel` rather than a claim about reka internals, correctness stops depending on a producer detail that is already untrue. defects.defect: The published `@mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0` declares `@mkbabb/glass-ui@^7.0.0` and `@mkbabb/keyframes.js@^6.0.0` as RUNTIME dependencies, while glass-ui declares `@mkbabb/value.js@^4.0.0` as a peerDependency — a package-level cycle, and the exact cycle eslint rule inv-K-1 exists to forbid, declared in the one file inv-K-1 does not police. The published graph imports neither; every downstream consumer of a parse/convert library installs 5.8 MB of Vue design system.
defects.evidence: package.json:82-85 `"dependencies": {"@mkbabb/glass-ui": "^7.0.0", "@mkbabb/keyframes.js": "^6.0.0"}`. `grep -rn "@mkbabb" src/` → 2 doc comments, 0 imports. `grep -h "^import" dist/subpaths/*.js | sort -u` → 6 lines, all relative internal chunks, ZERO bare package specifiers. vite.library.ts:13 `export const libraryExternal: string[] = [];`. eslint.config.js:211-213 inv-K-1 forbids src/→glass-ui by rule. `grep -rn "@mkbabb/keyframes" src demo test e2e scripts plugins` → 0 hits repo-wide. glass-ui/package.json peerDependencies includes `"@mkbabb/value.js": "^4.0.0"`. `du -sh node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui node_modules/@mkbabb/keyframes.js` → 5.2M / 608K.
defects.mechanism: the demo lives inside the library's own package manifest, so demo-only dependencies are indistinguishable from library dependencies; the invariant is enforced on the import graph (eslint) but not on the manifest, and the manifest is what npm resolves.
defects.reproduction: `npm pack` then inspect: files:["dist"] ships nothing importing either package, yet `npm i @mkbabb/value.js` in a fresh tree installs glass-ui + keyframes.js (5.8 MB) and creates a resolution cycle back to value.js via glass-ui's peer. Verified statically by the four measurements above rather than by a live install.
defects.proposedCure: Immediate: move both entries to `devDependencies` — nothing in the published graph resolves them, `files:["dist"]` ships nothing that needs them, and the generated self-alias set (vite.config.ts:38-51) is untouched. Structural (preferred): make `demo/` a private workspace package with its own manifest, so the demo's dependency set cannot leak into the library's published one by construction — the same class of guarantee the repo already chose for the exports-derived alias set.

defects.proposedCure: Split EmptyState into EmptyPlate + ErrorPlate (see L-4), then have ErrorBoundary COMPOSE ErrorPlate, retaining only what is genuinely its own: onErrorCaptured, aria-live="assertive", tabindex=-1 + focus(), and the reset emit. The four drifted numbers converge by construction.

defects.defect: EmptyState is two components under one name. `variant` is a flat optional prop over an all-optional prop record, not a discriminated union; the two branches share nothing but the flex wrapper (role=status vs role=alert, disjoint prop sets), and the seam leaks outward as an identical 12-line error+Retry block repeated at six call sites.
defects.evidence: EmptyState.vue:75-91 — message/variant/eyebrow/hint/detail/dots all independently optional; `dots` defaults true on a variant with no dots. Branches at :18-31 (role="alert") and :32-63 (role="status"). The component's own header comment at :2-3 says "TWO species, never conflated". Six duplicated call sites: AdminAuditPanel.vue:42-53, AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:22-33, AdminNamesPanel.vue:30-41 and :80-91, AdminTagsPanel.vue:68-79, AdminUsersPanel.vue:51-62, BrowsePane.vue:61-78.
defects.mechanism: species-as-flag — two disjoint components fused behind one name and a boolean-ish discriminator, so the type system cannot express which props are legal and the shared affordance (retry) has no owner, forcing every consumer to re-author it.
defects.reproduction: The six-fold call-site duplication is directly reproducible by the cited greps. The type-hole half — `<EmptyState variant="error" eyebrow="x" hint="y" dots />` compiling clean while silently dropping three props — is a HYPOTHESIS read off the flat optional prop record at :75-91; I did not execute vue-tsc to confirm the compile (pretypecheck runs a full library build).
defects.proposedCure: Two components in one home: EmptyPlate.vue (role=status; eyebrow/display/hint/#action; owns the ghost trio and its scale ramp) and ErrorPlate.vue (role=alert; glyph/display/detail; props {message, detail, retryLabel}; emits retry). Retire `variant` outright — no alias, no shim. The six copies collapse to `<ErrorPlate message="…" :detail="x.loadError.value" @retry="x.load()" />`, deleting ~72 lines of duplicated template and the six per-instance font-display Button overrides with them.

defects.defect: Inverted dependency: the tree's most-shared presentational leaf reads two custom properties that exist ONLY as inline properties imperatively written by the app-shell boot, and guards them with a masking fallback whose masked value is a known WCAG failure the component's own comment measured at 3.84:1.
defects.evidence: EmptyState.vue:45-47 `color="var(--accent-live)"`; EmptyState.vue:100-104 `.plate-ink { color: var(--ink-muted, var(--muted-foreground)); }`. Writers: demo/color-picker/composables/boot/useAtmosphereBoot.ts:96 and :103 (`document.documentElement.style.setProperty`). `grep -rn "ink-muted" demo/styles/; echo $?` → 1 (no declaration anywhere in the stylesheet layer). Live chromium probe: {"cascade":"oklch(44.712054906087% 0.003861589952 34.629978305623deg)","inline":"oklch(44.712054906087% 0.003861589952 34.629978305623deg)"} — byte-identical, the cascade contributes nothing. The masked value's cost is recorded by EmptyState.vue:45-49 itself: "the STATIC text-muted-foreground composited 3.84:1 over the My Palettes plate in light (< the 4.5:1 small-text floor)".
defects.mechanism: component → app-shell-boot edge carried over a CSS custom-property side channel, so no import exists and no lint, typecheck or module-graph tool can see it; the masking fallback (owner edict 2, explicit) then silently restores the exact defect the class was created to cure whenever the writer has not run.
defects.reproduction: `grep -rn "ink-muted" demo/styles/` returns nothing while the token is live at runtime — proving it is inline-only. Script: /private/tmp/claude-504/-Users-mkbabb-Programming-value-js/6614e90c-8bd6-434f-b017-5ad4277c6e5e/scratchpad/probe-token.mjs. The fallback FIRING is a HYPOTHESIS: in the live dev boot the writer runs before DOMContentLoaded (measured), so the exposure is the first-paint window plus any mount outside App.vue's boot scope (isolated unit mount, or the gh-pages prod-preview empty-mount already carried in CARRY-LEDGER.md §F) — neither of which I reproduced.
defects.proposedCure: Declare --ink-muted in demo/styles/foundation.css :root with the correct literal, exactly as that file already does for --accent-live at :231. The boot writer then OVERRIDES a declared token instead of ORIGINATING an undeclared one; delete the fallback outright. The leaf→boot edge becomes a cascade contract that holds in every mount context, and --ink-muted stops being the one token in the design system with no home.

defects.defect: `.plate-ink` — the concept "apply the certified de-emphasis rung to text" — is copy-pasted byte-identically into five separate scoped <style> blocks, each with its own 4-8 line rationale comment, while demo/styles/utils.css sits there as the demo's declared utility home.
defects.evidence: `for f in <5 files>; do grep -A2 "^\.plate-ink" $f | md5; done` → ade540e9e300d50d6dbe02bc25dfe2ae five times. Sites: demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue:102, demo/color-picker/ErrorBoundary.vue:84, demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractWorkbench.vue:290, demo/workbenches/extract/ImageDropZone.vue:109, demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractControls.vue:148. defects.reproduction: The md5 command above; five identical hashes.
defects.proposedCure: One `.plate-ink` in demo/styles/utils.css with one rationale comment; delete all five scoped blocks. Cleaner still: fold the rung into the demo's typography scale so `text-mono-caption` / `text-mono-small` carry it and `.plate-ink` disappears entirely.

defects.defect: PaletteCardGrid is a wrapper whose entire content is a rename: it re-declares EmptyState's API under an `empty*` prefix (4 props + 1 slot forwarded 1:1), giving the empty-plate concept two public surfaces, and fixes the card grid's job as knowing about emptiness.

defects.defect: Per-instance styling where the design system should speak: 11 `class="font-display"` overrides on <Button>, six of them inside EmptyState `#action` slots; and the ghost trio's whole scale/opacity ramp hard-coded as three per-instance Tailwind pairs.

defects.reproduction: The grep above; and reading EmptyState.vue:45-47, where the 8/11/6 + 0.8/1/0.6 ramp appears only as literal classes.

Move the trio ramp onto EmptyPlate as a single `trioScale` (or into the plate tokens beside --ink-muted), so the register is one edit. defects.defect: glass-ui publishes 74 subpaths and no ./empty-state, so the design system's empty/error primitive lives in the consumer — but lifting this component wholesale would move project-specific typography and owner-ratified copy INTO the design system, a worse ownership error than the one it cures.
defects.evidence: glass-ui@7.0.0 package.json#exports enumerates 74 keys including ./status-dot, ./badge, ./card, ./metric, ./pulse, ./completion-seal, ./watercolor-dot — and no ./empty-state. defects.defect: The `shared/` bucket that houses the tree's most-shared UI atom is named for a layer rather than a concept, holds exactly three files, and its charter is "things with no home" — including a deliberate fork of the library's own `debounce`.
defects.evidence: demo/shared/ contains only utils.ts, ui/PaneHeader.vue, ui/EmptyState.vue. demo/shared/utils.ts:9-22 documents the fork: "The utility tail has no rightful subpath home … so the demo owns its copy; the library's root-barrel export stands for external consumers." Every EmptyState consumer imports it by a deep relative path up to `../../../shared/ui/EmptyState.vue` (e.g. PaletteCardGrid.vue:36, AdminTagsPanel.vue:118) — there is no barrel.
defects.mechanism: layer-named residue bucket — owner edict 3's prohibition on new shared/ dirs is aimed at exactly this shape; the debounce fork is defensible on its own bundle-cost terms but confirms the directory's charter.
defects.reproduction: NONE for the fork (it is intentional and reasoned). The bucket's composition is directly observable via `find demo/shared -type f`.
defects.proposedCure: Dissolve demo/shared/: EmptyState → demo/plate/ (with a barrel, so call sites import "…/plate" not a 3-deep relative .vue path), PaneHeader → demo/shell/, utils.ts → demo/lib/. No bucket named for a layer survives.

result.strongestDefect: L-1a — the glass-ui `tag` prop boundary drift. glass-ui 7.0.0 (`490cc46e`) deleted `WatercolorDot`'s `tag?: "div" | "button"` prop, replaced `<component :is="tag">` with a hard `<span aria-hidden pointer-events:none>`, and added `defineOptions({ inheritAttrs: false })` forwarding only class/style. value.js adopted glass 7 whole at W44/D58 (`91fa1368`) and left 18 `tag=` bindings across 9 demo files unmigrated — three of them at EmptyState.vue:45-47. In EmptyState the delta is cosmetic (a dead prop, a false comment, a redundant aria-hidden — edict 2 legacy). Through the identical mechanism at the three `tag="button"` sites (MixSourceSelector.vue:164-176, :210-221, GenerateControls.vue:199-208) it is a BLOCKER: measured live, `.add-slot-ghost` renders `{tagName:"SPAN", ariaLabel:null, tabIndex:-1, pointerEvents:"none", ariaHidden:"true"}` and `.focus()` is a no-op — three shipped user-facing controls (add-to-mix, add-color-from-palette, copy-color) are inoperable and invisible to assistive tech. This is the strongest because it is a real, currently-shipping functional break; it was produced purely by reading the library boundary this seat was chartered to interrogate; and no gate the repo runs can see it, because `inheritAttrs:false` makes a stale binding a silent no-op with no DOM attribute, no lint error and no type error.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so this is not a negative verdict — but the following were hunted and came back clean, and one of them is load-bearing. (1) THE PUBLISHED-SURFACE AXIS IS CLEAN. The brief warns that a demo import a real consumer could not write is a false proof of the public API. EmptyState imports `@mkbabb/value.js` nowhere, and the whole demo consumes it only through published subpaths: `grep -rhn 'from "@mkbabb/value.js[^"]*"' demo/` → 49 imports across exactly 5 of the 7 exported subpaths (color 24, css 10, easing 5, math 6, quantize 4); `grep -rn '"@src' demo/` → 0; `grep -rn 'from "\.\./.*src/' demo/` → 0. Zero deep-src reach, zero alias use. T.W1's demo-dogfood keystone holds under adversarial grep — the library-structure defects reported here are in the MANIFEST and the DESIGN-SYSTEM boundary, not in value.js's own public surface. (2) NOT A GOD MODULE: 105 lines, 6 props, 2 slots, 2 imports, zero composables, zero stores, zero side effects, zero lifecycle hooks. Nothing to decompose but the two-species conflation. (3) NO INVERTED OWNERSHIP INTO src/: no library module knows anything about empty states; the reverse direction of the ownership question is clean. (4) THE NAMED HISTORICAL SUSPECTS DO NOT TOUCH THIS COMPONENT: no local useLayerTransition reimplementation, no palette export/serializer dual path, no third useDark store in EmptyState or either of its two imports. (5) VISUAL, ALL 60 SAFARI CAPTURES (audit/visual/REPORT.md): blankOrNearBlank 0, pageErrors 0, horizontalOverflow 0, darkClassMissing 0, mainCountNotOne 0. Every EmptyState-bearing route settles (browse 3595/3470 ms, palettes 3139/3443 ms, admin/* 3427-3506 ms). I read safari-desktop-light/admin-tags.png and safari-desktop-dark/browse.png as images: the plate renders correctly in both schemes, and in the dark Browse capture the two species sit side by side on one screen — the error statement ("The commons is unreachable." / "Failed to load palettes" / Retry) beside the empty invitation (neutral-dash ghost trio + "· EMPTY PLATE ·" + hint) — visibly distinct registers. The Q6 two-species design intent IS achieved on screen. It is achieved despite the structure, not because of it, which is why every defect above required evidence a screenshot cannot produce. (6) Also verified: only the report file was written — `git status --short src demo api test e2e` → clean; no INBOX, no scripts/dev/dev.sh, no vnext touched.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) for demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`, matching the explicit declaration this seat was spawned with. Not inherited, not undeclared.
result.strongestDefect: L-1 — PaneHeader derives its condensed title rung in-component via `calc(tan(atan2(--type-heading, --type-display-1)))` (PaneHeader.vue:140-142). A type-scale relationship was re-derived trigonometrically in a leaf component, promoting a browser's math-function implementation into a design-system input. WebKit mis-carries the angle unit in nested trig, so the ratio is 0.310808 on Safari vs 0.618029 on Chromium — measured live in both engines, and isolated to a 5-declaration CSS repro. Consequence on Safari desktop: the scrolled pane title lands at 41.888px × 0.310808 = 13.02px effective, below the 25.9px legibility floor this repo's own sibling grammar (demo/picker/header.css:87-93, BR-11/T-42) explicitly protects. Consequence on Safari mobile 390: the comment's "deliberate no-op" INVERTS to a 1.433843× enlargement — the title grows 324→465px wide, 27→39px tall, inside a 390px viewport, while Chromium correctly holds 1.0. Cure: the concept "one golden rung down" is a token step, which glass-ui already ships (card-scroll.css: [data-slot=card-title] display-2 → display-1). Delete the trig.
result.negativeProof: The `@mkbabb/value.js` published-surface axis is genuinely CLEAN and I proved it rather than passing over it. PaneHeader.vue has ZERO imports — its entire `<script setup>` is `defineProps<{ description?: string }>()` (:34-38), so there is no import edge to violate. Demo-wide: `grep -rhn 'from "@mkbabb/value.js' demo/ --include=*.ts --include=*.vue | sed 's/.*from //' | sort | uniq -c` yields exactly 49 imports across 5 subpaths (24 ./color, 10 ./css, 6 ./math, 5 ./easing, 4 ./quantize), every one a subset of the 7 published `exports` keys backed by src/subpaths/*.ts. `grep -rn 'from "\.\./\.\./\.\./src/\|value.js/src' demo/` → no output (zero deep-path reaches). `grep -rn 'from "@mkbabb/value.js";' demo/ test/ e2e/` → no output (zero bare-barrel reaches). No demo import exists that a real external consumer could not write. Also proved a second negative to stop the jury chasing it: glass-ui's veil carries `border-radius: inherit` and PaneHeader's does not, but measured `headerRadius: "0px"` / `veilRadius: "0px"` in both engines — `.pane-header` has no radius for the pseudo to inherit, so no corner artifact exists. NOT a defect.

defects.defect: The condensed title rung is derived by a browser trigonometric function inside a leaf component — `--pane-title-shrink-ratio: calc(tan(atan2(var(--type-heading), var(--type-display-1))))`. A type-scale relationship whose home is the token layer was re-derived in-component, making each engine's math-function implementation a design-system input. WebKit produces 0.310808 where Chromium produces 0.618029: the Safari pane title shrinks to 13.02px effective (below the 25.9px BR-11 floor the repo's own sibling grammar protects), and on Safari mobile the documented "self-neutralizing no-op" inverts to a 43% ENLARGEMENT.
defects.evidence: demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue:140-142 (the calc); comment claim at :132-139 ("CLOSED-FORM... ≈0.618 (1/φ) at the ≥1440 cap, degenerating to exactly 1 on phones"). MEASURED live, /#/about @1440x900, host scrolled to 200: webkit `matrix(0.310808,…)` title 462px→144px; chromium `matrix(0.618029,…)` title 462px→286px; both report identical `--type-heading: 1.618rem`, `--type-display-1: clamp(1.618rem, 1.2rem + 1.6vw, 2.618rem)` computed 41.888px, `supportsSDA: true`. MOBILE 390x844 /#/gradient: `webkit REST {"tr":"matrix(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0)","w":324,"h":27} STUCK {"tr":"matrix(1.433843, 0, 0, 1.433843, 0, 0)","w":465,"h":39}` vs `chromium STUCK {"tr":"matrix(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0)","w":324,"h":27}`. MECHANISM isolated to 5 CSS declarations, no app: a=`tan(atan2(1.618rem,2.618rem))` webkit 310.797px / chromium 618.016px; b=`tan(31.71776deg)` 618.031px BOTH; c=`tan(31.71776rad)` 311.344px BOTH; d=`atan2(1.618rem,2.618rem)/1deg` 31717.27 BOTH; e=`tan(atan(0.618))` 618px BOTH. webkit a == c ⇒ atan2() returns a correct angle (row d) but tan() consumes its numeric value as radians. Arithmetic: 31.71727 − 10π = 0.301343 rad; tan(0.301343) = 0.31081 = measured to 5 figures. Floor it violates: demo/picker/header.css:87-93. Only atan2 site in the repo: `grep -rn atan2 demo/ src/` → PaneHeader.vue:141.
defects.mechanism: wrong-home: a design-system concern (type-scale relationship) re-derived inside a demo leaf component, so engine-dependent CSS math becomes a design input
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaneHeader/probe-L-structure.mjs (dev server live on :9000) for the app measurement; the 5-declaration isolation and the 390px mobile inversion scripts are pasted verbatim in the report's Reproduction section
defects.proposedCure: ARCHITECTURAL TRANSPOSITION, not a patch: delete the trig and the `transform: scale()` entirely. "One golden rung down from display-1" is a discrete token step and belongs in the design system, where glass-ui already expresses it — dist/components/card/card-scroll.css steps `[data-condensed] > [data-slot=card-title]` from `--type-display-2` to `--type-display-1` with no math function, no @supports gate, and no per-engine evaluation. Under the L-2 cure this defect cannot exist: there is no calc() and no scale() left to get wrong.

defects.defect: Triplicate ownership of one concept, with the canonical home sitting unused in node_modules. glass-ui 7.0.0 — adopted WHOLE at V·W44 — ships `CardHeader shrink` with the veil, the sufficiency-gated threshold crossing, the title token step, the description collapse, and a prefers-reduced-motion arm. The demo carries TWO forks of it (PaneHeader.vue for 9 panes; useHeaderCondense.ts + picker/header.css Row B for 1), and the premise that justifies both — that the producer's grammar is "compositor-only BY ARCHITECTURAL COMMITMENT" and "structurally cannot satisfy §0.8/BR-9" — is FALSE against 7.0.0, which transitions `padding-block-start` and steps `font-size`: real layout channels.
defects.evidence: False premise: demo/picker/composables/useHeaderCondense.ts:9-15. Refutation, node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/card/card-scroll.css (full text): `.card-header--shrink { transition: padding-block-start var(--duration-normal) … }`, `[data-condensed="true"] { padding-block-start: var(--card-header-pad-condensed) }`, `[data-condensed="true"] > [data-slot=card-title] { font-size: var(--type-display-1) }`, `[data-condensed="true"] > [data-slot=card-description] { display: none }`, `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { … transition: none }`. Producer mechanism, dist/card-Bk96VI2R.js `__name: "CardHeader"`: `o.value?.closest(".card-scroll-host")`; gate `e.scrollHeight - e.clientHeight > t.getBoundingClientRect().height/2 + 24`; `triggers: [{at:24,direction:"down",id:"condense"},{…"expand"}]`; `watch(f, g, {immediate:!0, flush:"post"})`. Fork B equivalent: useHeaderCondense.ts:65-73 (overflowY auto|scroll ancestor walk), :80 (`opts.threshold ?? 24`), :94-98 (`overflow <= savings + threshold`, `savings = expandedH - expandedH*0.5`), :75,121 (`{immediate:true, flush:"post"}`) — same algorithm, same constant 24, same flush. Producer has ZERO demo consumers: `grep -rn "card-scroll-host" demo/` → no output; `grep -rn shrink demo/ | grep -i cardheader` → nothing. Dep is `"@mkbabb/glass-ui": "^7.0.0"`; adoption commit 91fa1368. Duplication volume: PaneHeader.vue 224 lines + useHeaderCondense.ts 127 lines + picker/header.css:48-143 ≈ 96 lines ≈ 447 demo-owned lines.
defects.mechanism: wrong-home: a design-system primitive hand-forked into demo/, twice; the forks survived their own supersession when 7.0.0 was adopted whole (edict-2 legacy/dual-path)
defects.reproduction: cat node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/card/card-scroll.css; cat node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/card/CardHeader.vue.d.ts; node -e 'const s=require("fs").readFileSync("node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/card-Bk96VI2R.js","utf8"); const i=s.indexOf("CardHeader"); console.log(s.slice(i-60,i+900))'; grep -rn "card-scroll-host" demo/
defects.proposedCure: Retire both forks; PaneHeader.vue ceases to exist. Nine panes become `<Card tier="resting" class="card-scroll-host …"><CardHeader shrink><CardTitle as="h2">Title</CardTitle><CardDescription>…</CardDescription></CardHeader><CardContent>…</CardContent></Card>`. Where 7.0.0 is genuinely short of §0.8 the delta goes UPSTREAM to glass-ui as a CardHeader variant/knob via the standing BH relay (edict 4) — it does not come back into demo/. Before landing, two things must be MEASURED not re-quoted: (1) the §0.8/BR-9 claim against 7.0.0's actual padding+font-size grammar; (2) the picker's specific readout line-lock / blob-reservation geometry, which is Fork B's own seat.

defects.defect: Physical `transform-origin: left top` in a document that ships a deliberate RTL seam. Under dir=rtl the visually right-aligned title box collapses toward physical left, so the title detaches from the very edge it is aligned to and drifts 342px inward, ending mid-header while the header's right edge stays put. LTR is pinned, which is why it was never seen.
defects.evidence: demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue:184 `transform-origin: left top;` (and the comment restating it at :156). RTL is a supported seam: demo/color-picker/index.html:6 documents the `dir` seam explicitly, and the mega-tranche visual audit captures shots/rtl-desktop/ + shots/rtl-mobile/. I read shots/rtl-desktop/gradient.png: pane titles "Gradient" and "My Palettes" render right-aligned as required. MEASURED, dir=rtl @1440x900 /#/about: rest → header {l:200,r:710}, title {l:224,r:686}, transformOrigin "0px 0px"; scrolled 200 → header {l:200,r:710}, title {l:224,r:368}. Title right edge 686 → 368 = 342px drift away from its alignment edge; header right edge unchanged at 710. LTR control, same probe: title l:754 at BOTH states (pinned). Chromium rtl reproduces the same left-anchored collapse (r:686 → r:510, 286px box).
defects.mechanism: wrong-home: physical-axis geometry hand-written in a demo leaf, where the design system uses a direction-agnostic token step that has no origin to get wrong
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaneHeader/probe-L-structure.mjs — the dir="rtl" rows for both engines print titleRect before/after scroll alongside the ltr control
defects.proposedCure: Subsumed by L-1/L-2 and that is the point: a `font-size` token step shrinks a text box from its own inline-start by construction, in either direction, with zero origin declaration. No `scale()` survives the transposition, so RTL becomes correct by construction rather than by a second `[dir=rtl]` override.

defects.defect: Inverted, untyped, silently-failing cross-boundary contract. A leaf component in demo/shared/ui/ publishes a GLOBAL class `.pane-scroll-fade` from an unscoped <style> block, which each of its nine ANCESTOR panes must independently remember to apply — no import edge, no prop, no type, nothing vue-tsc or eslint can see. The failure mode is byte-identical to a legitimately dormant state, so no test can catch a future omission. And glass-ui already owns the identical declaration under a different name.

result.strongestDefect: C-1 — the title's "closed-form" shrink ratio `calc(tan(atan2(var(--type-heading), var(--type-display-1))))` (PaneHeader.vue:140-142) is built on an identity WebKit does not implement for font-relative lengths: WebKit feeds `tan()` the DEGREE magnitude of `atan2()`'s angle and consumes it as radians. Measured exact to 6 s.f. across three independent cases (tan(atan2(1rem,1rem)) -> 1.619775 vs required 1; tan(atan2(2rem,1rem)) -> 0.688691 vs 2; tan(atan2(1.618rem,2.618rem)) -> 0.310808 vs 0.618029; px operands correct in both engines). Two shipping consequences: desktop Safari lands the stuck title at 31% instead of the designed 62%; and on iPhone 14 — where the file's comment (:136-138) claims the ratio "degenerates to exactly 1 ... the shrink self-neutralizes" — the title instead GROWS to matrix(1.619775), box 324x27.2 -> 524.8x44 inside a 356px header on a 390px viewport, painting straight over the TYPE/SPACE/HUE select row (screenshot committed). The `@supports (animation-timeline: scroll())` gate cited as protection does not protect: this WebKit build satisfies it while getting atan2 wrong.
