result.strongestDefect: L-1 (carried from pass 1, independently CONFIRMED this pass): `tag=` is dead at the glass-ui boundary — `grep -o "tag" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js` returns ZERO occurrences in the shipped 7.0.0 bundle, yet EmptyState.vue:45-47 still pass `tag="div"` three times, part of 18 surviving bindings across 9 files that glass 7's `inheritAttrs:false` swallows with no DOM attribute, no warning and no type error. Strongest NEW finding of this pass: N-1 — the `dots` prop is a dead configuration axis with zero call sites, unreachable through PaleteCardGrid's renaming wrapper from the one plate that carries a second ghost register (measured live: two registers at 48px and 44px), modelling a condition that cannot occur anywhere in the tree, and contradicted by a certified e2e oracle (o9-shadow-palette.spec.ts:265-269) that requires the trio present exactly where the prop would shed it.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, but four structural hypotheses this challenge's premise predicts came back CLEAN and are recorded so no downstream wave "fixes" them: (1) THE IMPORT GRAPH IS SOUND IN BOTH DIRECTIONS — EmptyState's entire import surface is two lines (EmptyState.vue:69-70), `@lucide/vue` (a declared glass-ui peer, 47 demo files) and `@mkbabb/glass-ui/watercolor-dot` (a real key in glass-ui's 74-key exports map — a granular published subpath a real consumer could write verbatim, NOT a deep path); demo/shared/ has 24 inbound and ZERO outbound edges into any feature, shell or boot module, its complete outbound set being lucide, glass-ui/watercolor-dot, clsx, tailwind-merge. No feature→shell, no component→boot, no demo→src/ internal edge exists. (2) VALUE.JS'S PUBLIC SURFACE HOLDS UNDER ADVERSARIAL GREP — EmptyState imports value.js nowhere, and the whole demo consumes it only through published subpaths (/color x25, /css x10, /math x6, /easing x5, /quantize x4; zero `@src` alias use, zero `../src/` reach). Extended this pass to the RESOLUTION level, which pass 1 did not run: `tsc --traceResolution` against the real tsconfig.demo.json (evidence/resolution-trace.txt) shows `@mkbabb/value.js/css` — which has NO tsconfig paths entry and is imported 10x — resolving via TypeScript SELF-NAME RESOLUTION through the repo's own package.json#exports to the LOCAL build at /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/dist/subpaths/css.d.ts, not to the installed 4.0.0 self-copy (whose css.d.ts is 1,580 bytes smaller). The demo-dogfood trust boundary is intact on all 7 subpaths; the tsconfig drift of N-5 is inert. (3) NO BESPOKE EMPTY-STATE BYPASSES THE COMPONENT — scanning every .vue matching seven empty-phrase patterns and filtering to files that do not reference EmptyState returns the empty set; the EMPTY species genuinely has one home (only the ERROR species is forked, N-2). (4) ATTRIBUTE FALLTHROUGH ACROSS THE ROOT v-if/v-else WORKS — the one thing about this two-root template that could silently fail; measured on the rendered DOM, the EmptyState root under PaletteCardGrid carries "…gap-2.5 py-8 text-center col-span-full", hasColSpanFull: true, role "status". Also re-confirmed from pass 1: no god module (105 lines, 6 props, 2 slots, 2 imports, zero composables/stores/side-effects/lifecycle), no src/ module doing this component's job, neither named historical suspect (useLayerTransition reimplementation, third useDark store) touches this component, and the 60-capture Safari matrix reports blankOrNearBlank 0 / pageErrors 0 / horizontalOverflow 0 / darkClassMissing 0 / mainCountNotOne 0 with both species rendering correctly in light and dark.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue, area core)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`, the tier declared at spawn. Seat declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D-1 — with two palettes saved, typing a non-matching search query renders "· empty plate · / No saved palettes yet. / Add colors above, then save the set." plus the canon-restricted TRUE-EMPTY mark, while the pane heading 400px above simultaneously reads "My Palettes ②". The component asserts a statement the same viewport disproves, because it exposes one `message` for two distinct states (true-empty vs filtered-zero) and PalettesPane.vue:77 binds `:empty` to the FILTERED collection length.

defects.defect: The empty plate cannot distinguish a true zero from a filter-induced zero, so a populated library renders the true-empty invitation and asserts a falsehood the adjacent header badge numerically refutes.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:77-80 (`:empty="pm.filteredSaved.value.length === 0"` + empty-text="No saved palettes yet."). Live probe D2-probe7.mjs: with 2 seeded palettes, populated={plate:null,cards:2}; after query "zzzzqqqq" -> filteredZero={plate:{text:"· empty plate ·No saved palettes yet.Add colors above, then save the set.",role:"status",hasTrio:true},cards:1}. Screenshot probes/probeD-filtered-zero-populated.png shows heading "My Palettes ②" above the plate. Same mechanism at BrowsePane.vue:83 and AdminUsersPanel.vue:63. Canon VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:186 reserves the EmptyPaletteMark for TRUE empty; :114 puts filter-zero in the count/status jurisdiction.
defects.mechanism: Missing state in the species taxonomy — one `message` prop and a two-member `variant` union cannot express WHY the collection is zero, so the consumer cannot make the distinction no matter how careful it is.
defects.reproduction: Seed localStorage["color-palettes"]={version:1,palettes:[2 local palettes]} (key at demo/palettes/usePaletteStore.ts:6) -> load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes -> type "zzzzqqqq" into the "Search your palettes…" input. Script: scratchpad/D2-probe7.mjs; capture probes/probeD-filtered-zero-populated.png.
defects.proposedCure: Replace `variant`+`message`+`eyebrow`+`hint`+`dots` with a discriminated union modelling the REASON: {kind:"empty"} | {kind:"filtered";query;total} | {kind:"failed";detail;retry} | {kind:"unavailable"}. The mark then rides `kind==="empty"` structurally and cannot leak; the filtered arm carries the count and a Clear action.

defects.defect: The failure species exists only as a full content REPLACEMENT, so a failed refresh hides list data that is still retained in state, on 6 sites across 5 Admin routes.
defects.evidence: EmptyState.vue:14 (v-if error) / :28 (v-else) are sibling roots — no non-destructive form exists. Consumers order error before the list: AdminTagsPanel.vue:68 -> :82 -> :85; same at AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:22, AdminAuditPanel.vue:42, AdminUsersPanel.vue:51, AdminNamesPanel.vue:30 and :80. Composables retain the data on catch: useAdminTags.ts:53-59 sets loadError but never clears tags.value; identical at useAdminFlagged.ts:69-75 and useAdminAudit.ts:63-67. BrowsePane.vue:62 is the lone site that invented the guard (`&& displayedBrowse.length === 0`). Canon PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:52 PR-08 and VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:101.
defects.mechanism: Missing fourth species — failure-with-retained-data. The component offers only 'replace the region with an error plate', so 6 of 7 consumers destroy visible truth on a routine Refresh.
defects.reproduction: SOURCE-DERIVED and exact: template order (v-if=loadError precedes the v-else list) + composable retention (tags.value/items.value untouched in catch). NOT rendered — this dev host cannot reach the failure branch (see D-19): probing #/browse logged exactly one non-asset request (GET http://localhost:9000/), and the Admin composables early-return at useAdminTags.ts:50 `if (!token) return;`.
defects.proposedCure: The `failed` register becomes a bounded status STRIP above retained rows carrying Retry; only a failure with nothing to retain escalates to a full plate (the `unavailable` arm of D-1's union). This deletes the ad-hoc guard from all seven consumers.

defects.defect: The `--ink-muted` de-emphasis rung that carries the whole caption/statement hierarchy is 6.4x weaker in dark than in light — in dark the hierarchy is effectively gone.
defects.evidence: Rendered-pixel measurement (PIL scan of probes/probeD-{light,dark}-trio-crop.png, #/admin/users 1440x900): light plate rgb(243,189,206), eyebrow ink rgb(86,84,83)=4.65:1, headline rgb(28,25,23)=10.81:1 -> ratio-of-ratios 2.32x. Dark plate rgb(121,78,89), eyebrow rgb(221,218,217)=4.96:1, headline rgb(233,230,226)=5.54:1 -> 1.12x. OKLCH L separation: light |0.2161-0.4471|=23.10 L-points; dark |0.9262-0.8900|=3.62 L-points; 6.38x. Also visible in the tracked matrix ../../visual/shots/safari-desktop-dark/admin-tags.png. Canon PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:73.
defects.mechanism: The certified rung is specified as a contrast FLOOR only (EmptyState.vue:49-54, :95-101). In dark the floor-clamp drives the caption up to within 3.6 OKLCH L-points of --foreground; there is no ceiling obligation, so the rung stops separating.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/D2-probe2.mjs (contrast_light / contrast_dark blocks) then the PIL row-scan of the two trio crops; both under docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/EmptyState/probes/.
defects.proposedCure: Give --ink-muted a paired SEPARATION obligation at the boot writer (useAtmosphereBoot.ts:85,103): clamp to the plate AND hold >=12 OKLCH L-points from --foreground in the same scheme, resolving conflicts by moving the plate rather than the ink. Closes for all 33 consumers of the token at once.

defects.defect: The ornament is painted with `--accent-live`, an INK-contrast-guarded token, used in a specimen/paint slot — costing 8.95x chroma in dark, so the mark stops reading the live accent that is its entire stated purpose.
defects.evidence: EmptyState.vue:45-47 pass color="var(--accent-live)"; foundation.css:221 documents it as "the contrast-guarded LIVE picked color". Computed: light oklch(47.119% 0.188448 9.834deg), dark oklch(95.832% 0.021053 9.834deg) -> C 0.1884 vs 0.0211 = 8.95x loss, L 0.471 -> 0.958. Rendered dot background: light color(srgb 0.6655 0.0001 0.2617/0.12), dark color(srgb 0.9999 0.9247 0.9331/0.12). Same-frame proof: ../../visual/shots/safari-desktop-dark/admin-tags.png renders the EmptyState trio achromatic white while the sibling "Start a new palette" ghost dot 150px above stays pink. The correct token family already exists — ExtractControls.vue:124 uses safeCss(cssColor, GRAPHICS_CONTRAST_FLOOR).
defects.mechanism: Ink-guard vs graphics-guard confusion: contrast-guarding for TEXT drives lightness to whichever pole reads against the plate, which annihilates chroma for anything used as paint.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/D2-empty-probe.mjs — tokens block for light and dark; compare probes/probeD-light-trio-crop.png with probeD-dark-trio-crop.png.
defects.proposedCure: Specimen/ornament paint resolves through a GRAPHICS floor (GRAPHICS_CONTRAST_FLOOR), never the ink guard. One token swap at the producer seam.

defects.defect: In dark the aria-hidden ornament is the highest-contrast element on the plate — the decoration outranks the message.
defects.evidence: Combines D-3 and D-4: dark message contrast 5.54:1 while the 44px mark carries a hard 2px dashed edge at near-white oklch(95.8%) over a plate at OKLCH L 0.395 (probes/probeD-dark-trio-crop.png). In light the mark is the only saturated element on the plate (probeD-light-trio-crop.png). Canon VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:34 (one full-strength protagonist; supporting fixtures do not compete) and PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:70 (decoration without information is not on the permitted-mark list).
defects.mechanism: The mark's contrast is bounded below (legibility) but never bounded above relative to the caption it sits over, so scheme changes reorder the visual hierarchy.
defects.reproduction: Open probes/probeD-dark-trio-crop.png and probeD-light-trio-crop.png side by side at 1:1.
defects.proposedCure: Bound the mark's rendered contrast ABOVE by the caption rung: ghost stroke drops to the caption rung and its chroma comes from the graphics floor (D-4), so it reads as atmosphere rather than as an edge.

defects.defect: `dots` defaults true, so the canon-restricted EmptyPaletteMark ships on all 5 Admin routes; the escape-hatch prop has zero consumers.
defects.evidence: EmptyState.vue:90 `{ variant:"empty", eyebrow:"· empty plate ·", dots:true }`. `grep -rn "dots" demo/ --include=*.vue` returns only the definition (EmptyState.vue:37,40,88,90) plus the unrelated GradientEasingEditor `specimen-dots` — zero call sites pass it. All 10 empty-variant sites therefore render the mark, incl. AdminUsersPanel.vue:63,138 / AdminTagsPanel.vue:82 / AdminAuditPanel.vue:56 / AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:37 / AdminNamesPanel.vue:42,92. Canon scopes the mark to the palette field (VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:186) and zeroes ornament elsewhere (PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:49 PR-05; VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:218). ../../visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/admin-tags.png shows the identical mark twice in one viewport at the same scale.
defects.mechanism: An opt-OUT default for a canon-restricted ornament: the permissive default ships the mark everywhere and the restriction is documented only in a comment (:29-38) that nothing enforces.
defects.reproduction: grep -rn "dots" demo/ --include=*.vue ; then open ../../visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/admin-tags.png.
defects.proposedCure: Default false, then delete the prop: the mark becomes a structural consequence of `kind==="empty"` AND a palette-field host per D-1's union. The ten-line N-3 comment block goes with it.

defects.defect: The canon names a primitive `EmptyPaletteMark`; it does not exist in glass-ui 7.0.0, so it is hand-rolled from three inline WatercolorDots whose stroke weight and dash rhythm do not scale with diameter.
defects.evidence: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:186 names it; `ls node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui@7.0.0/dist/components/ | grep -iE "empty|mark"` returns only `handmark`. EmptyState.vue:39-48 inlines it as w-8/w-11/w-6 + opacity-80//opacity-60. glass-ui.css `.watercolor-ghost-stroke { border: var(--watercolor-ghost-weight,2px) dashed … }` and `--watercolor-dash:8px/--watercolor-gap:5px` are fixed -> 2px is 8.3% of the 24px dot's diameter vs 4.5% of the 44px (1.8x heavier edge on the small dot) and ~5.8 vs ~10.6 dashes around the perimeter. The producer's own scaling seam `container-type: inline-size` is bypassed by the fixed w-* utilities. Breaches owner edicts 4 and 5.
defects.mechanism: A composed mark is expressed as three per-instance utility overrides in a consumer instead of one primitive that owns its own proportional relations.
defects.reproduction: Read node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/glass-ui.css (.watercolor-ghost-stroke, .watercolor-swatch) and EmptyState.vue:39-48; inspect probes/probeD-light-trio-crop.png at 1:1 — the small dot's ring reads heavier than the large one's.
defects.proposedCure: Land `EmptyPaletteMark` in glass-ui as the canon already names it — owning the three diameters, a proportional --watercolor-ghost-weight/dash pair, aria-hidden, and the graphics-floored accent. EmptyState renders one tag; D-4, D-8 and D-15 close with it.

defects.defect: One 10px gap token serves four semantic ranks; the rendered ink rhythm is 14 : 23 : 16 and it INVERTS the canon's title-gap / section-gap relation.
defects.evidence: gap-2.5 at EmptyState.vue:16 and :28 is the only vertical relation. Box gaps measured exactly 10px between all four children (D2-probe5.mjs offsets from plate top: trio 32-76, eyebrow 86-107.58, headline 117.58-153.17, hint 163.17-186.14). Per-row ink scan of probes/probeD-inkscan.png (DPR 1, 462x218, threshold dLuma>18): bands (32,75)(90,100)(124,149)(166,181) -> rendered gaps 14px / 23px / 16px. Canon PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:68 requires distinct title vs section gaps; :73 requires the rendered relation to govern.
defects.mechanism: A single flex `gap` across three different font metrics (Fira 14.38/21.58, Fraunces 25.89/35.60, Fira 16.4/22.96) — half-leading differs per pair, so a uniform box gap cannot produce a uniform ink gap. Result: the eyebrow is optically bonded to the ornament (14px) and detached from the statement it labels (23px).
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/D2-probe5.mjs (inkGeo block) then the PIL row-scan of probes/probeD-inkscan.png.
defects.proposedCure: Trim the line boxes so token == ink (`text-box: trim-both cap alphabetic` on the three text rows), then split into two tokens: --empty-title-gap (eyebrow->statement, tight) and --empty-section-gap (mark->eyebrow, statement->action, phi larger).

defects.defect: `max-w-[26ch]` on the Fraunces display line is 46% looser than authored, because `ch` samples the display serif's lining figure rather than its average glyph.
defects.evidence: EmptyState.vue:20 and :58. Computed at 1440: font-size 25.888px, max-width 469.474px -> Fraunces ch = 18.06px = 0.698em. Rendered average advance: "No saved palettes yet." = 22 chars in 272.84px = 12.40px/char. 469.474/12.40 = ~38 characters permitted against an authored 26. The two Fira Code rows are exact (36ch->363.32px at 10.09px/ch; 44ch->444.06px) because they are monospace. Side effect: the hint's honest 36ch measure (363px) is NARROWER than the headline's nominal 26ch (469px).
defects.mechanism: `ch` is font-relative and is being used as a character-count proxy in a proportional display face where `0` is 46% wider than the mean advance.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/D2-empty-probe.mjs — kids[].maxWidth and kids[].w for the headline row on #/admin/users at 1440.
defects.proposedCure: Author display measures in `em` of their own face or as a token (--measure-display: 22em); retain `ch` only on the monospace rows.

defects.defect: `font-display text-heading` is a Fraunces<->text-heading family/size mapping that the closed type matrix does not contain, plus two per-instance overrides on a root-owned utility.
defects.evidence: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:66-78 publishes the matrix and closes it ("closed across all eighteen compositions … P019's pair is the SOLE exception"), mapping text-heading -> Plus Jakarta Sans. EmptyState.vue:20 and :58 render `font-display text-heading` — measured fontFamily "Fraunces", fontSize 25.888px, fontWeight 700. Per-instance overrides on the same root utility: `leading-snug` (rendered line-height 35.596px = 1.375, overriding text-heading's producer-hardcoded leading noted at foundation.css:379) and `text-balance`. Blast radius: EmptyState.vue:20, :58, ErrorBoundary.vue:24, Markdown.vue:26 — 4 sites, 3 of them copies of this plate. Owner edict 5.
defects.mechanism: A genuinely new type role was created by pairing a family utility with a size utility, rather than being named in the matrix or resolved to an existing rung.
defects.reproduction: grep -rn "font-display text-heading" demo/ --include=*.vue ; node scratchpad/D2-empty-probe.mjs for the computed family/size/leading.
defects.proposedCure: Either the matrix names this 18th role explicitly, or the statement line drops to --type-subheading (Fraunces, already in the matrix) and the leading/balance overrides move to the root utility.

defects.defect: The file's own claim to be "the ONE shared empty atom" is false — the failure plate is cloned twice more with every proportion nudged, and the scoped .plate-ink rule is duplicated verbatim.
defects.evidence: EmptyState.vue:98 makes the claim. ErrorBoundary.vue:16-33 re-types the same plate with drift: glyph w-6 h-6 -> w-7 h-7, gap-2.5 -> gap-3, py-8 -> py-10 px-6, max-w-[26ch] -> [28ch], max-w-[44ch] -> [46ch]; and EmptyState.vue:102-104 is duplicated verbatim at ErrorBoundary.vue:84-86. Markdown.vue:20-29 is a third rendering via Alert+AlertTitle whose comment asserts it joins the register "verbatim" while being a fourth geometry. Owner edicts 1 and 3.
defects.mechanism: An abstraction was declared in a comment and then not used — three incompatible geometries each carrying a comment asserting shared-ness.
defects.reproduction: diff the class strings: sed -n '14,27p' demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue vs sed -n '16,33p' demo/color-picker/ErrorBoundary.vue vs sed -n '20,29p' demo/scenes/about/markdown/Markdown.vue.

WebKit feeds atan2's DEGREE magnitude to tan() as RADIANS for font-relative operands, and because --type-display-1 is a viewport-fluid clamp the resulting value is an unbounded, sign-changing, POLE-CROSSING function of viewport width. Measured live on http://localhost:9000/#/, WebKit: 10.868346x at 1024px, -0.363219 at 1180, -0.642357 at 1200, -1.587175 at 1240, -7.39094 at 1280, +13.171055 at 1300, +3.42998 at 1320, 0.310808 at >=1440 — correct at ZERO of the 20 widths probed, while Chromium is correct at all 20. defects.defect: The title-shrink ratio is built on the CSS identity tan(atan2(y,x)) === y/x, which WebKit does not implement for font-relative lengths — it feeds atan2's degree magnitude to tan() as radians. Because --type-display-1 is a viewport-fluid clamp, the shipped value is an unbounded, sign-changing, pole-crossing function of viewport width on WebKit. At 1024px the pane title renders at 10.87x and covers the entire pane; at 1280px it renders mirrored and off-screen, taking the About pane's colour-space <button> (slotted inside the <h3>) with it.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt (demo/color-picker/ErrorBoundary.vue)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`. Explicitly declared at spawn, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: V-1 — a plain network failure on a lazily-imported pane chunk replaces the ENTIRE application with a bare "Try again" button on an empty gradient field, permanently. No injected code is required: `usePaneRouter.ts:69-78` declares ten `defineAsyncComponent(() => import(...))` with no errorComponent/loadingComponent/timeout, so the fetch rejection reaches the single boundary at App.vue:50 that wraps the whole two-pane grid. Measured with `page.route("**/BrowsePane.vue**", r => r.abort("failed"))`: paneContainer false, boundary caught. It then composes with C-1 (the decorative aurora canvas paints OVER the boundary's static text — headline contrast 1.12:1, zero glyph pixels in the text boxes) so nothing but the button renders, and with C-2 (the `caught` latch has no key, watcher or route coupling) so the field stays dead across every subsequent route. The component's own header comment says it exists so the app is "NEVER a silent white-screen dead plate"; evidence/V1-chunk-abort.png is that dead plate, in pink, with a button on it.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so this field records the negatives I PROVED rather than assumed, since the brief named specific local hazards to check. (1) No `defineModel` — the two pieces of state are plain `ref`s read only by this component's own template, so the WritableComputedRef async-round-trip stale-read hazard cannot apply. (2) The file imports nothing from `src/` — no colour maths, no `ValueUnit` wrapping, no `stableHue`, no parsing; the oklch→HSV hue-drift, ValueUnit-nesting and `parseCssColor` crash classes are all structurally absent. (3) `grep` over the SFC: no `requestAnimationFrame`, no timers, no `addEventListener`, no observers, no WebGL — nothing to leak, and the PRM-RAF epidemic does not touch this file; the single `nextTick` callback is `?.`-guarded and self-terminating. (4) No unbounded growth: `detail` is one string, overwritten not appended. (5) No reka-ui slider, so no pointer-capture leak. (6) Zero per-frame/per-keystroke/per-tick work — in the healthy path the component renders `<slot/>` and one HTML comment (unit probe C-F output pasted in the report), i.e. it is completely inert until it catches. (7) Tap target and accessible name are clean: measured 124×36 px with the name "Try again", above the 24 px floor — the component contributes nothing to the visual REPORT's smallTapTargets (60) or nameless-button counts, though only because `grep -in "Try again" audit/visual/REPORT.md` returns nothing, i.e. the visual matrix never captured the error state at all.

defects.defect: Total diagnostic blackout. `return false` at :68 makes Vue's handleError return before app.config.errorHandler and before logError; the component logs nothing itself and emits nothing on catch. The hook signature additionally discards Vue's `instance` and `info` arguments, and the app installs no global net at all, so the error reaches no channel anywhere.
defects.evidence: demo/color-picker/ErrorBoundary.vue:59 (`onErrorCaptured((err) => {` — instance and info dropped), :68 (`return false`). Unit probe C-B, my run: `console.error mentioning the throw: false`, `console.warn mentioning the throw: false`, `app.config.errorHandler invocations: 0`, `component emissions on catch: {}`. Live: with INDUCED-AUDIT-THROW caught, the full session console+pageerror capture contains zero mention of it. `grep -rn "errorHandler|unhandledrejection|window.onerror" demo/` returns only ErrorBoundary.vue:67's own comment; demo/color-picker/index.html:210 calls createApp(App) with no config.errorHandler. Contradicts the honesty contract App.vue:144-149 preserves elsewhere.
defects.mechanism: propagation suppression conflated with observability suppression — two separate decisions taken by one `return false`
defects.reproduction: `npx vitest run --config docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/ErrorBoundary/probes/vitest.challenge-c.config.ts` and read the [C-B] stdout block.
defects.proposedCure: Log before suppressing: take the full hook signature `(err, instance, info)` and put `console.error("[ErrorBoundary]", err, info)` immediately above the `return false`. Suppressing propagation to the app root and destroying the only record of the failure are different decisions and this file conflates them.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model ID `claude-opus-5[1m]`. The tier was explicitly declared in my spawn prompt and matches the model I observe myself to be; nothing inherited, no substitution.
result.strongestDefect: D2-1 — the failure register's legibility is a free variable of user input. The plate has no material tier, so its ground is the seed-tinted ambient field while its ink is bound to the colour scheme; the two are independent, so no ink value satisfies all grounds. Measured across four seeds: the failure statement drops to 1.89:1 on a dark seed (below even the 3.0 large-text floor at Fraunces 25.888px/w700), and the destructive glyph — the only non-textual failure register — fails the 3.0 floor at ALL four seeds, worst 1.10:1 on a crimson seed where the semantic failure hue collides with the user's own hue and the alert glyph dissolves into the field. No token, alpha or media arm can close a contrast whose ground is unbounded user input.
result.negativeProof: Not SOUND. Positive findings recorded as evidence, not as absence of a finding: (1) the sole recovery control measures 159.2 x 54 CSS px at 390x844 with accessible name "Try again" — meets44:true, notable because REPORT.md reports smallTapTargets on all 60 captures elsewhere in the app (evidence-r2/R2-measurements.json -> mobileTap); (2) the only animated properties in the caught state are background-color, border-color, box-shadow, color, opacity, scale at 0.2s — all paint/composite, none layout-forcing (R2-measurements.json -> motion.button); (3) Vue 3.5 idioms are correct on all three counts — useTemplateRef (ErrorBoundary.vue:57), reactive props destructure with defaults (:43-51), type-only defineProps/defineEmits — and are MORE current than the withDefaults in the atom it copies (EmptyState.vue:72); (4) verbatimModuleSyntax has nothing to violate — lines 39-41 import only runtime values; (5) producer provenance is respected: demo/ui/button/index.ts is one line, `export { Button } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";`; (6) 87 lines, single purpose, no god module, no aliases, no dual paths, no back-compat arms; (7) `return false` in onErrorCaptured (:68) correctly halts propagation to app.config.errorHandler.

defects.defect: The failure register's legibility is a free variable of the user's seed colour. The plate paints directly on the seed-tinted ambient aurora field with no material tier, so ink (scheme-bound) and ground (seed-bound) vary independently.
defects.evidence: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/ErrorBoundary/evidence-r2/R2-measurements.json -> seeds. Measured composited backdrops (ink hidden, exact rect screenshot-clipped and averaged): default seed statement rgb(28,25,23) on rgb(242,92,163) = 5.69:1, glyph rgb(219,36,36) = 1.60:1; crimson #e11d48 statement 3.92:1, glyph 1.10:1; paper #fafaf9 statement 7.01:1, glyph 1.96:1; ink #0b1020 statement 1.89:1, glyph 1.86:1. Statement is Fraunces 25.888px w700 (R2-paint.json -> meta.fonts.msg) = large text, floor 3.0; glyph is a graphical object, floor 3.0. Frames evidence-r2/R2-seed-crimson-lifted.png and R2-seed-ink-lifted.png. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §2 'One surface has one tier' and 'Seed tint is forbidden outside the ambient field...'; §4.1 'Text, focus, boundaries and state meet their rendered contrast on the actual material tier; a token name is not evidence' — against ErrorBoundary.vue:12-14 and :79-86, 22 lines offering token names as evidence.
defects.mechanism: F1 — an unratified composition: the fallback replaced the stage instead of occupying a seat, so it inherited the seat's obligations without its material tier.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/ErrorBoundary/r2-probe.mjs (dev server live at :9000). Recipe: page.route(/AboutPane\.vue/, r => r.abort('failed')); page.goto('http://localhost:9000/#/?space=hex&color=%230b1020') at 1440x900 WebKit; wait 9s; the boundary is up.
defects.proposedCure: Seat the fallback on a real producer material so its ground is the neutral Structural-glass / Specimen-well family the constitution defines. glass-ui@7.0.0 exports ./surface and ./card (verified in its package.json exports). The architectural form of this is D2-7's cure: render the fallback INSIDE the pane seat, which supplies the tier automatically and needs no new token.

defects.defect: The plate's ink paints under the atmosphere canvas: in the shipped caught state the glyph, the failure statement and the machine-truth detail contribute zero pixels. The user sees one wordless glass pill in an empty field.
defects.evidence: evidence-r2/R2-paint.json. Shipped state, ZERO page mutation: statement rect (16,020 px sampled) has 0 pixels within RGB distance 60 of its own ink rgb(28,25,23), min luma 128.0; glyph rect (784 px) 0 near-ink px, min luma 128.7; button rect 237 near-ink px (5.309%), min luma 25.5 — only the button paints. Two mutually exclusive interventions each restore it: boundary position:relative -> statement 3,089 px (19.282%); canvas display:none with boundary left static -> statement 3,016 px (18.826%). Computed styles: boundary/msg/svg position:static zIndex:auto; btn position:relative; canvas position:absolute covering 1440x900. Frame evidence-r2/R2-shipped-desktop-1440-light.png vs R2-lifted-desktop-1440-light.png. defects.mechanism: Demo-only dependencies were declared as runtime `dependencies` instead of `devDependencies` on a package whose `files` ships only `dist`. In-repo the hazard is masked because vite.config.ts:40-50 aliases the seven specifiers to the local dist before node resolution runs.

defects.proposedCure: Two subtractive moves. (1) Make stampStops(stops) a computed alongside truncated/visible — the component already has that exact pattern two lines above; the template call is the only un-memoized read in the file. (2) Hosts hand the chip a computed keyed on (count, seed, preset, harmony) instead of calling the truth function in the template — the row list is fixed and the truth function is pure and seeded, so one computed map serves every open. If pass-1's C-1 cure is taken and the cap moves to the host, both fall out for free: the host computes the stops it wants shown once, and the chip paints exactly what it is handed.

Measured: Retry does re-invoke the loader but cannot recover, and the only affordance that would work — a page reload — is not offered.

Probe R2-B: {"probe":"R2-B","caught_on_load_failure":true,"detail_shown":true,"loader_attempts_after_retry":2,"still_announced_after_retry":true,"pane_present_after_retry":false,"text_after_retry":"This panel hit an unexpected error.Failed to fetch dynamically imported module Try again"}.
defects.mechanism: A generic boundary cannot distinguish 'this render is broken' from 'this build is stale', because the discriminating information lives in the async loader it does not own. So it offers one affordance for two classes and it is wrong for one of them — and it shows the user machine truth for the wrong machine ('Failed to fetch dynamically imported module'). NOTE, recorded honestly: I predicted defineAsyncComponent memoisation would make Retry a no-op; measured, attempts went 1→2, so the loader IS re-invoked. The prediction was wrong; the defect is not.

result.strongestDefect: L2-1 — containment owned at one fixed altitude that is wrong in both directions. Round 1's latch and this round's uncontained shell are one defect seen from two sides: a component whose lifetime is the application's holds a fact about a pane, while the shell's own failure is owned by nobody. Fixing either half alone leaves the other; only the transposition (pane containment into PaneSlot keyed on liveKey, shell containment above App at the mount site, reporting in a boot module) dissolves both. L2-2 is its enabling condition — until demo/color-picker/main.ts exists there is no module in which the shell half or the reporting layer can be written at all.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, but these axes are genuinely CLEAN and the positive evidence is recorded so no later seat re-litigates them. (1) No deep-path library reach: ErrorBoundary.vue:39-41 is exactly three imports — vue, @lucide/vue, ../ui/button. No @mkbabb/value.js, no @src/*, no path into src/. An external consumer holding vue + @lucide/vue + @mkbabb/glass-ui could write this file verbatim. CAVEAT RECORDED, NOT WITHDRAWN: the axis is clean but its instrument is broken (L2-4) — the demo's declared view of the published surface names three files that do not exist and omits two subpaths that do, so 'the demo proves the public API' is vacuous for all 88 component seats until that is generated. (2) No src/-belongs logic and no library code doing this component's job: nothing in the 87 lines is colour, parsing, maths, easing or transform. (3) Not a god module: 87 lines, one responsibility per file, no composables of its own. (4) verbatimModuleSyntax has nothing to violate — every imported binding is a value (ref, nextTick, onErrorCaptured, useTemplateRef, CircleAlert, RotateCcw, Button); there is no type-only import to have mis-declared. (5) Vue 3.5 idioms correct: useTemplateRef<HTMLElement>("alertRef") at :57 (not the legacy same-name ref), reactive props destructure with defaults at :43-51, typed defineEmits<{reset:[]}>() at :53. (6) None of the named historical suspects touch this file: no local useLayerTransition reimplementation, no usePaletteExport/export-serializers dual path, none of the three parallel useDark stores — it imports no composable at all. (7) @lucide/vue as a devDependency is the correct declaration: glass-ui declares it peerDependencies {"@lucide/vue":"^1.16.0"} and package.json#files is ["dist","!dist/gh-pages","!dist/gh-pages/**"], so the demo is never published. (8) The plate itself is correct when it paints — role="alert" + aria-live="assertive", tabindex=-1 with nextTick focus, a visible affordance; the U-F58 a11y contract genuinely shipped. Across the 4x15=60-capture Safari matrix the boundary never fired: pageErrors 0, blankOrNearBlank 0, one console error (safari-desktop-light /#/: WebGL: context lost.) which is the async class no boundary can catch. The defect is never that the plate is wrong — it is that the plate is at the wrong altitude, in a directory that is simultaneously the entry and a shared library, offering an affordance that does not work, with nothing beneath it.

result.strongestDefect: D-1 — the F7/F8 inset hairline ring, the component's entire declared boundary law, is NEVER PAINTED: CSS paints an inset box-shadow below in-flow descendants, and PreviewStrip fills its padding box with opaque segment children. Proven by controlled A/B in the live document at DSF 4 with an identical resolved shadow value (C1 payload-on-self = 1.00 CSS px ring band; C2 payload-in-child = zero ring pixels), with the live component matching C2 in light and dark on both hosts. The sibling PreviewRamp, same class name and same docblock law, does get its ring because its payload is a background-image on the element. The prior seat measured this as "the ring is too faint" (1.23–1.75:1); that reading is wrong in the component's favour — the ring is absent, so every bleed-through failure the docblock claims it mitigates is unmitigated.
result.negativeProof: Genuinely sound, attacked and survived: (1) MOTION — `grep -nE "transition|animation|@keyframes|will-change|transform" PreviewStrip.vue` returns nothing; no animated property, none layout-forcing, so `prefers-reduced-motion` needs no arm and owner edict 6 is not engaged (`git log -- PreviewStrip.vue` shows one commit, `a61094e3`, a tree move — no animation was ever deleted). (2) Vue 3.5 idiom (edict 7) — `const { stops } = defineProps<…>()` is correct reactive props destructure; no template ref, no `defineModel`, so `useTemplateRef`/`shallowRef` do not apply. (3) `verbatimModuleSyntax` (edict 8) — both imports at :21-22 are value imports; `sample.ts:27-33` correctly marks its four type-only imports. (4) God modules (edict 1) — 76 lines, one job, four-symbol barrel. (5) Legacy (edict 2) — no aliases, shims, dual paths or masking fallbacks. (6) Zero colour math in the view: stops arrive pre-computed and are stamped verbatim on `data-stops`; that separation is right and should survive any cure. (7) Overflow priority — `flex: none` on the plate + `min-w-0` on the wrapper truncates the description, never the specimen; measured `overflowX = 0` at 320 px. (8) `aria-hidden` on a decorative colour plate is correct on `/generate` where the row carries name + text description. (9) Idle cost — the menu unmounts closed, so the chips cost nothing at rest; no page errors on `/generate`.

defects.mechanism: CSS paint order: an element's inset box-shadow paints above its own background but BELOW its in-flow descendants. The colour payload lives in opaque child spans that fill the padding box (clipped to the same rounded rect by overflow:hidden), so the shadow is occluded by the component's own content. PreviewRamp escapes only because its payload is a background-image on the element itself.

result.strongestDefect: D-2 — the "four-arc quartet" the design exists to draw can never be four arcs. `HUE_INDEX` (src/color/anchors.ts:360-366) covers only {hsl,hsv,hwb,lch,oklch}, so for the 4 non-polar spaces of the 9 offered (oklab, lab, rgb, xyz) the `hue` option is a total no-op and all four Hue-method ramps are byte-identical; and even in polar spaces increasing/decreasing collapse onto shorter/longer, capping distinct previews at 2 — never 3, never 4. The app's DEFAULT space is `oklab` (useMixingState.ts:44), so in the shipped default configuration the Hue-method menu shows four different labels over four identical chips while the Select stays enabled. This is the purest design defect: it was provable at design time from the library, it teaches the user a falsehood, and it survives every fix to the co-blocker D-1. (D-1 — zero instances render, own e2e oracle RED — is the shipping blocker of record.)

defects.defect: The four-arc hue quartet can never render four distinct arcs. In the 4 non-polar spaces of 9 (oklab, lab, rgb, xyz) all four hue ramps are byte-identical; in polar spaces increasing/decreasing collapse onto shorter/longer, capping distinct previews at 2; achromatic operands collapse all four to 1 in every space. The app's default space is oklab, so the shipped default shows four labels over four identical chips with the Hue-method Select still enabled and offering a choice that provably cannot change the result.
defects.evidence: src/color/anchors.ts:360-366 `export const HUE_INDEX = { hsl: 0, hsv: 0, hwb: 0, lch: 2, oklch: 2 }`; src/color/operations.ts:101-111 applies interpolateHue only `if (i === hueIndex)`. demo/color-session/color-space-meta.ts:26-36 offers 9 spaces. demo/workbenches/mix/composables/useMixingState.ts:44 `const colorSpace = ref<PickerSpace>("oklab")` — confirmed visually in both Safari /mix screenshots (trigger reads "OKLab"). defects.mechanism: preview untruth — a differentiating affordance whose differentia is structurally absent; the menu's shape (4 flat rows) does not match the domain (polar-ness of the space × orientation of one operand pair)
defects.reproduction: node /tmp/pr_probe3.mjs (shipped sampler algorithm verbatim vs dist/subpaths/color.js, operands #e11d48→#0ea5e9) → `oklch 2 differ / oklab 1 *** ALL FOUR IDENTICAL *** / lab 1 *** ALL FOUR IDENTICAL *** / lch 2 / hsl 2 / hsv 2 / hwb 2 / rgb 1 *** ALL FOUR IDENTICAL *** / xyz 1 *** ALL FOUR IDENTICAL ***`. node /tmp/pr_probe4.mjs → `oklch #e11d48→#0ea5e9 distinct=2 groups=shorter=decreasing longer=increasing`; `oklch #111111→#eeeeee distinct=1 groups=shorter=longer=increasing=decreasing`.
defects.proposedCure: Transpose the vocabulary, do not patch the chip. (1) INTERPOLATION_SPACES gains `polar: boolean` derived from the library's single source (the HUE_INDEX keyset); when the selected space is non-polar the Hue-method row is disabled with a named reason and leaves the tab order — the lane says why instead of showing four lies. (2) In a polar space, expose the two real trajectories as two, naming the direction for the current pair ("Shorter — counter-clockwise for these colors"), so increasing/decreasing read as the orientation restatement they are rather than as two further arcs. This is a subtraction.

defects.defect: The "one golden plate (φ² ≈ 2.618rem)" proportion is φ² at NO viewport the app ships. `inline-size: 2.618rem` is root-relative and viewport-invariant; `block-size: 1em` is font-relative and rides the fluid text-dropdown rung, so the plate's aspect ratio is a function of viewport width.
defects.evidence: demo/color-session/color-chips/PreviewRamp.vue:43-44 (`inline-size: 2.618rem; /* one golden plate — φ² × 1em (F7) */` + `block-size: 1em`). Measured live on /#/mix with the Color-space menu open: desktop-1440 lane 16.4px → 41.875×16.391px, aspect 2.5548 (−2.41% vs φ²=2.6180339887); mobile-390 lane 14px → 41.875×14.000px, aspect 2.9911 (+14.25%); mobile-320 identical (+14.25%); zoom-200 lane 14.6px → 41.88×14.59px, aspect 2.869 (+9.6%). Canon: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:73 §5.8 "Real rendered relation wins over token intent … token presence alone cannot close a row."
defects.mechanism: unit-family mismatch — a ratio asserted across two different length bases (rem vs em) so it holds only where root font-size equals inherited font-size, which never happens at this site
defects.reproduction: node /tmp/pr_live7.mjs  (navigates http://localhost:9000/#/mix at 1440/390/320, opens the Color-space Select, injects a span carrying PreviewRamp's exact declarations into each option's description lane, reads getBoundingClientRect) → the three-row table above. node /tmp/pr_states.mjs supplies the zoom-200 row.
defects.proposedCure: One sized axis, one unit family: `block-size: 1em; aspect-ratio: 2.618;` (or `inline-size: calc(1em * 2.618)`). The ratio then holds by construction at every clamp arm and cannot drift when the type rung is retuned.

defects.mechanism: contrast by token-faith — an alpha chosen for aesthetic quietness and asserted to perform a boundary job, never measured against either neighbour it must separate

defects.proposedCure: A single-tone 12% ring cannot bound an arbitrary colour against arbitrary translucent glass; the problem is scheme-symmetric so the answer must be. Draw a two-tone hairline — an inner --background-derived stroke and an outer --foreground-derived stroke, each at the alpha that clears 3:1 against its own neighbour — which is the construction glass-ui already ships on .watercolor-swatch (`inset 0 0 6px …background 35%…, inset 0 -2px 4px …foreground 6%…, 0 2px 6px …foreground 10%…`). One ring, both schemes, no per-scheme override.

defects.defect: O-14's own doctrine is re-admitted between samples. sample.ts forbids CSS gradient interpolation "because the preview must show what THE APP computes, not what the browser's engine would"; PreviewRamp then paints `linear-gradient(90deg, …)` with no `in <space>`, so 16 of 17 segments of the chip's width are the browser's default (oklab) interpolation — in every row, regardless of which of 9 candidate spaces the row previews. The e2e guard checks only the stop LIST, so the forbidden mechanism is present and unmeasured.
defects.evidence: sample.ts:5-11 states the law. PreviewRamp.vue:25 `linear-gradient(90deg, ${stops.join(", ")})` — no interpolation space declared. e2e/smoke/oracles/o14-preview-truth.spec.ts:360-392 asserts only `painted.length === stamped.length` plus per-component equality of the DECLARED stops. Measured painted pixel vs a direct mixColors recompute at each segment midpoint (RGB Euclidean 0–255, chip rendered at 100× width): hsl/longer worst 15.6 at segment 5 (painted 217,216,23 / library 228,227,24); hsv/longer worst 15.6; oklch/longer worst 5.1 (painted 89,162,10 / library 88,162,5).
defects.mechanism: doctrine leak — the module's stated prohibition is enforced at the sample points and abandoned everywhere between them, with the oracle blind to the gap
defects.reproduction: node /tmp/pr_o14b.mjs — builds the 17-stop list with the shipped sampler algorithm against dist/subpaths/color.js, paints it as a linear-gradient in Chromium, screenshots and decodes the strip in-page, samples the midpoint pixel of each segment and compares to mixColors at the same t.
defects.proposedCure: Choose one and say so. Either paint hard segments as PreviewStrip does — the divergence becomes identically zero and the two components collapse toward one grammar — or state honestly in the docstring that the chip is a 17-sample approximation whose inter-sample paint is the UA's, and add a midpoint leg to the oracle with a declared tolerance.

defects.defect: An unreachable guard, and the absence law owned in two places. `v-if="stops.length >= 2"` can never evaluate false because the sampler returns either null or an array of length ≥ 2; the host already guards on the same fact. Two guards, one reachable — a masking fallback — and "honest absence" therefore has two owners and no owner.
defects.evidence: PreviewRamp.vue:31 `v-if="stops.length >= 2"`. sample.ts:69 `const perSegment = Math.max(2, Math.ceil(k / segments) + 1);` and :74 pushes perSegment stops for segment 0, so a non-null return always has ≥2 stops; sample.ts:58 `if (operandsCss.length < 2) return null;`. Host guards: MixConfigBar.vue:111 `v-if="spaceRamps.get(s.value)"` and :133 `v-if="hueRamps.get(m.value)"`. Owner edict 2 (no masking fallbacks).
defects.mechanism: masking fallback — a defensive condition that cannot fire, duplicating a law the caller already enforces, so neither site owns it
defects.reproduction: NONE — this is a static-reachability finding proved by reading sample.ts:58,69,74 against PreviewRamp.vue:31 and MixConfigBar.vue:111,133. No runtime input makes the inner v-if false while the outer guard is true.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the unreachable v-if and let the sampler's `null` be the single absence authority — which is what D-1's cure requires anyway, since the absence state must be DRAWN by one component rather than silently skipped by two.

defects.defect: RTL is undesigned. The gradient angle is a hardcoded physical `90deg` inside a component that is otherwise scrupulously logical (inline-size / block-size), the file has no [dir] handling, and the V canon records no direction ruling for the ramp although the constitution requires one per domain.
defects.evidence: PreviewRamp.vue:25 `linear-gradient(90deg, …)` vs :43-44 `inline-size` / `block-size`. PreviewStrip.vue:74 has the same shape plus a physically-anchored truncation mask `mask-image: linear-gradient(90deg, black 20%, transparent 95%)` that fades the visual right regardless of reading direction. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:150-154 §6.1 requires a per-domain direction rule; grep of the V canon returns no row for the chip (see D-8).
defects.mechanism: direction undesigned — a physical axis left unruled in a component whose sibling axes are all logical
defects.reproduction: HYPOTHESIS (labelled, unverified) for the rendered consequence: in RTL the operand rack (a flex row, MixSourceSelector.vue:121) reverses while the ramp does not, so the ramp's operand order would read against the rack's. My probe could not confirm it — setting dir="rtl" on documentElement after hydration did not flip the portaled listbox's computed direction (node /tmp/pr_states.mjs → "rtl": { "dir": "ltr" }). The ABSENCE of a recorded decision is proven from source and is the finding.
defects.proposedCure: Record the ruling, then encode it. If the ramp is an ordinal sequence tied to the operand rack, derive the gradient angle from the resolved inline direction (`to inline-end`, or a `[dir=rtl]` override) so ramp and rack agree; if it is a scientific axis that must stay literal per VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6.1, say so in the docstring and add the RTL frame to the evidence matrix. Either way it must be decided once, in canon, for both chips.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/color-session/color-chips/PreviewRamp.vue (and its module sample.ts), measured live against http://localhost:9000
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context variant). Declared at spawn, not inherited. No sub-agents spawned; every probe, command and screenshot in the report was produced by this seat.
result.strongestDefect: C-1 — PreviewRamp cannot render at all in the shipped app. Its sole host is MixConfigBar, whose chips are gated on >=2 mix operands; the only affordance in the entire UI that appends an operand is the mix add-slot ghost, which glass-ui 7.0.0 renders as `<span aria-hidden="true">` with `pointer-events: none`, `tabIndex -1`, no aria-label and no bound click handler (`inheritAttrs: !1` in node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js silently drops the consumer's `tag="button"`, `aria-label`, `@click`, `:disabled`). Measured: real mouse click and synthetic element.click() both leave `[data-mix-source]` at 0; all nine live option rows contain `<!--v-if-->` exactly where the chip would be. The component is dark code behind a dead door, and the only currently-GREEN browser test of it is the one asserting it is absent.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, but these arms were checked and are positively SOUND, with evidence: (1) the k-sample apparatus genuinely earns its keep — the forbidden shortcut (engine interpolates from the two endpoints) deviates from library truth by mean 116.67/max 185 (oklch·longer), 40.14/71 (hsv), 20.90/43 (xyz), 119.57/190 (hsl·longer) with 38-42 of 42 columns wrong (probe-C-paint2.mjs); (2) honest absence works exactly as documented — <2 operands, unparseable operand, "", and currentColor all return null, measured in-browser through the real module; (3) every named local hazard is absent by file read — no defineModel (no stale WritableComputedRef round-trip), no oklch->HSV roundtrip or stableHue (the chip does zero colour maths), no ValueUnit anywhere in the chain (readonly string[] only), no reka-ui slider/pointer capture, ZERO requestAnimationFrame (no PRM-RAF contribution), no WebGL, no direct parseCssColor; (4) no lifecycle and no leak surface — zero onMounted/onUnmounted/listeners/observers/timers/async/fetch; (5) reactivity is idiomatic Vue 3.5 reactive-props-destructure and fires correctly, neither too little nor too often; (6) verbatimModuleSyntax satisfied — both SFC imports are value imports, and sample.ts:27-33 marks all four type imports `type`; (7) accessibility contributes nothing to the visual REPORT tallies and could not — aria-hidden is correctly placed on a decorative element whose truth is carried by the option label + description, the component renders no interactive element, and the menu-open option hit rect measures 219x52.36 px; (8) no console or page errors on /#/mix in any probe, matching REPORT.md rows 123/138/153/168 (pageErr 0, consoleErr 0, overflowX 0).

defects.defect: PreviewRamp is unreachable in the shipped app: the only UI path that can supply its >=2 operands is a dead <span>. glass-ui 7.0.0's WatercolorDot declares `inheritAttrs: !1` and hard-codes `aria-hidden: "true"`, silently discarding the host's `tag="button"`, `aria-label`, `@click` and `:disabled`.
defects.evidence: probe-C-ghost.mjs: {"ghost":{"tag":"SPAN","pointerEvents":"none","ariaHidden":"true","tabIndex":-1,"hitIsSelfOrChild":false},"swatchesBefore":0,"swatchesAfterMouse":0,"swatchesAfterSynthetic":0}. probe-C-addslot.mjs: byRoleCount 0, anyAriaLabelMatch 0. probe-C-operands.mjs live option markup contains `<!--v-if-->` where the chip belongs, stopsEls 0 across 9 options. Source: demo/workbenches/mix/MixSourceSelector.vue:165-175 (declares tag="button" + aria-label + @click); chain demo/workbenches/mix/MixConfigBar.vue:111,133 -> MixPane.vue:103 -> useMixingState.ts:42,55-57 -> MixSourceSelector.vue:68-72. Producer: `grep -o 'inheritAttrs[^,}]*' node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js` -> `inheritAttrs: !1`.
defects.mechanism: Semantics (operability, name, handler, disabled) travel across a package boundary as Vue fall-through attributes into a component that opts out of attribute inheritance. Vue drops them with no type error, no runtime warning, no lint. A producer version bump turned an operable control into decoration and nothing in the build noticed.
defects.reproduction: node /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PreviewRamp/probe-C-ghost.mjs — or by hand: open http://localhost:9000/#/mix, click the dashed ghost in the Selected well; nothing is ever added, and the ghost is not tab-reachable.
defects.proposedCure: Producer-side, not a host patch: WatercolorDot must take an explicit `as`/`tag` prop and `v-bind="$attrs"` (or expose a real <button> wrapper slot) so the operability contract is part of its typed API and breaks the typecheck when it changes. This is a glass-ui change and therefore owes a BH-inbox relay (owner edict 4). Until it lands, the host owns the <button> and the dot is its decoration.

defects.defect: The only oracle for this component is RED, is textually unpassable even if it were reachable, and is not run in CI; the vitest file named for the chip tests only the sampler function.
defects.evidence: `npx playwright test e2e/smoke/oracles/o14-preview-truth.spec.ts --project=smoke -g "T-17 chip referent"` -> `2 failed / 1 passed`; both failures are `locator.click: waiting for getByRole('button', { name: 'Add current color to the mix' })` at :355 and :414; the passing test is :334 "honest absence: with <2 operands the rows carry NO chip". probe-C-paint2.mjs, feeding the spec's verbatim parseOklchTriples regex (o14-preview-truth.spec.ts:162-168): {"stampSample":"oklch(62% 0.27 9.8deg)","paintedTriples":17,"stampedTriples":0,"o14Assertion":"expect(painted.length).toBe(stamped.length)"}. `npx vitest run test/preview-chips.test.ts` -> 4 passed, all four call sampleInterpolationRamp, none mounts the SFC. `grep -n "run:" .github/workflows/ci.yml` -> npm ci / lint / vue-tsc x2 / build / npm test only; no playwright job exists.
defects.mechanism: The component's truth is asserted only about its input function (sample.ts) and only in a browser leg that is neither reachable nor runnable. `[\d.]+` in the oracle regex cannot cross the `%`/`deg` units the stamp dialect uses, while the computed background-image canonicalises to unitless — so stamped parses to 0 triples and painted to 17. The gate is vacuous in three independent ways at once.
defects.reproduction: Vacuous mutations that keep every gate green: change `linear-gradient(90deg, ...)` to `linear-gradient(180deg, ...)` (PreviewRamp.vue:25); change `stops.join(", ")` to `stops.join(" ")` (invalid gradient, chip paints nothing); change `v-if="stops.length >= 2"` to `>= 99` (PreviewRamp.vue:31); delete the entire <style> block. Run `npx vitest run` and CI after any of them — all green.
defects.proposedCure: Give the SFC a @vue/test-utils mount test in vitest (paint embeds exactly data-stops; <2 stops renders nothing) so CI's existing `npm test` step enforces the chip's own contract without depending on the mix flow being operable. Then make stampStops a genuine canonical serialisation so the browser leg's regex becomes a belt on a canonical form rather than the only thing holding the O-14 law up.

defects.defect: The paint violates the module's own SAMPLING LAW: `linear-gradient(90deg, ...stops)` uses POSITIONLESS stops, so the browser interpolates every pixel between library samples — in OKLab, regardless of the row's candidate space. The docblock's claim of "a discrete-stop linear gradient" is false; >=60% of the chip's painted columns are engine fill, and the result is measurably not the library's output.
defects.evidence: sample.ts:5-16 forbids it by name ("never CSS `in <space>` gradient interpolation ... no engine divergence") and sample.ts:16-19 says "a chip that approximates the library output is FORBIDDEN"; PreviewRamp.vue:6-7 claims "discrete-stop"; PreviewRamp.vue:24-26 is the positionless gradient. probe-C-paint.mjs interpolation control, endpoints oklch(0.62 0.27 20)/oklch(0.62 0.27 200) 180deg apart, midpoint pixels read from a real screenshot: default `linear-gradient(90deg,A,B)` -> [133,134,134] (OKLab-lerp prediction [135,135,135]); `in oklch shorter hue` -> [148,140,0]; `in srgb` -> [52,65,127]. probe-C-paint2.mjs, chip paint vs per-column library truth at the chip's real 42px width: hsl/longer max 15/255, mean 4.43, 16 of 42 columns >4; oklch/longer max 8/255; hsv max 2; xyz max 1. 17 stops across 42 columns means at most 17 columns can be library truth.
defects.mechanism: The sampler was built specifically to keep the browser engine out of the interpolation, then its output was handed to the engine as a CONTINUOUS gradient — the one CSS construct that puts the engine back in. The discretisation the docblock describes exists nowhere in the file. The sibling PreviewStrip implements the law correctly (per-segment background-color), which is why the divergence survived review: two chips, one law, only one of them implementing it.
defects.reproduction: node /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PreviewRamp/probe-C-paint.mjs (interpolation-space control, rows E/F/G) and node .../probe-C-paint2.mjs (chip-vs-library-truth table). Banked image: paint-probe.png.
defects.proposedCure: Emit the hard stops the docblock already claims — `stops.map((s,i) => `${s} ${i/n*100}% ${(i+1)/n*100}%`)` — which deletes the engine from the interpolation, makes the docblock true, collapses data-stops and the paint into one referent, and makes the ramp structurally identical to PreviewStrip. The gestalt version is the rooted chip plate: one primitive taking a stops list and a discrete|continuous intent, instead of two components that disagree about what "discrete" means. (If a genuinely continuous ramp is wanted, the sampling law must be amended and the row must declare its own space, e.g. `linear-gradient(in oklch longer hue ...)`, never silently inherit OKLab — that is a design ruling, not an implementation choice.)

defects.defect: Under `@media (forced-colors: active)` the chip paints nothing at all — background-image is stripped, background-color is transparent, the hairline ring is gone. `.preview-chip` is absent from the repository's own COLOR-SURFACE ROSTER and the component never sets the `[data-color-surface]` opt-in hook.
defects.evidence: probe-C-edge.mjs, a span carrying PreviewRamp.vue:40-49's exact declarations painted with a real sampler ramp: {"backgroundImage":"none","backgroundColor":"rgba(255, 255, 255, 0)","forcedColorAdjust":"auto","boxShadow":"none"}. Images: chip-normal.png (a ramp) vs chip-forced-colors.png (the page showing straight through — a transparent hole). `grep -n "preview-chip|data-stops|data-color-surface" demo/styles/*.css` -> only foundation.css:694 and :837, the two `[data-color-surface]` hooks; `.preview-chip` appears in neither roster (foundation.css:678-700 forced-colors, :800-840 print).
defects.mechanism: A named global policy with a generic opt-in hook that a later component forgot to opt into. The roster is a list, and lists rot — PreviewStrip (born in the same wave) has the identical omission, which is the argument for the hook rather than the list.
defects.reproduction: node /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PreviewRamp/probe-C-edge.mjs — or /#/mix in DevTools -> Rendering -> Emulate CSS media feature forced-colors: active.
defects.proposedCure: One attribute on the chip root: `data-color-surface`. `forced-color-adjust` inherits, so it covers both the forced-colors and print blocks in one move — no roster edit, no new selector, no per-instance override. Gestalt: put it on the single rooted chip plate so the next chip species inherits the policy instead of re-forgetting it.

defects.defect: The F7 "golden plate" law is false as written: `inline-size: 2.618rem` is root-anchored while `block-size: 1em` is inheritance-anchored, so the two axes resolve in two different font contexts. The measured ratio is 2.554, not phi-squared = 2.61803, and the chip is 19% taller than the description line it claims to join.
defects.evidence: PreviewRamp.vue:9-11 ("the chip joins the description line — height 1em, width one golden plate (φ² ≈ 2.618rem)") and :43-44 (`inline-size: 2.618rem; block-size: 1em;`). probe-C-paint2.mjs fontContext, measured at the chip's exact DOM slot with the menu open: {"wrapperFontSize":"16.4px","microFontSize":"11px","microLineHeight":"13.75px","microH":13.75,"nameFontSize":"16.4px","rootFontSize":"16px","chipWouldBe":{"wPx":41.888,"hPx":16.4}}. 41.888/16.4 = 2.554.
defects.mechanism: rem-vs-em anchor split: the comment's own arithmetic ("φ² × 1em") is only true when the inherited font size equals the root font size. It does not here (16.4px vs 16px) and would not under any user font-size override. Separately, the chip is a SIBLING of `.text-micro` (MixConfigBar.vue:110-113), not a descendant, so its `1em` resolves against the option's NAME lane (16.4px), never the description lane (11px/13.75px) — "joins the description line" was never true of the cascade.
defects.reproduction: node /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PreviewRamp/probe-C-paint2.mjs, section `fontContext`.
defects.proposedCure: Write the law in one unit against one anchor — `block-size: 1em; inline-size: 2.618em;` — so the plate is phi-squared by construction at every scale, and give the chip the font size of the lane it claims (`font-size: var(--text-micro)`, or move the chip inside the description lane). Do it once, in the single rooted chip plate.

defects.defect: `.preview-chip` is minted twice, in two disjoint scoped <style> blocks, and the two copies have already drifted.
defects.evidence: PreviewRamp.vue:40-49 vs PreviewStrip.vue:56-65. Identical: flex, inline-size 2.618rem, block-size 1em, border-radius var(--radius-sm), the inset color-mix hairline. Divergent: `display: inline-block` (ramp) vs `inline-flex` (strip); `overflow: hidden` present only on the strip; the F7/F8 rationale comment present only on the ramp.
defects.mechanism: A shared primitive implemented as a duplicated declaration block. Scoped styles mean the two copies can never collide, so nothing ever forced them to agree — and they already do not. The `overflow: hidden` divergence is not cosmetic: it is exactly the declaration the ramp would need if C-3's cure turned it into child segments.
defects.reproduction: Read both files; `grep -rn "preview-chip" demo/color-session/color-chips/`.
defects.proposedCure: Root the chip plate once as a glass-ui variant of the existing chip/swatch family (owner edicts 4 and 5 — the design system, not demo/ui/, and never a per-instance override): one recipe carrying geometry in one unit against one anchor (C-5), the ring, `data-color-surface` (C-4), and per-segment children (C-3/C-8). Being a glass-ui change it owes a BH-inbox relay before it lands.

defects.defect: `serializeStop`'s alpha normalisation `.replace(/ \/ 1\)$/, ")")` is dead code — it never matches any input the module can produce, and would not match the serialiser's actual alpha output if it ever fired.
defects.evidence: sample.ts:39-41. probe-C-edge.mjs over 9 spaces x 4 hue arcs x 17 stops = 612 serialisations: {"slash1Hits":{"hits":0,"total":612}}. Fed an explicitly alpha-1 colour, the serialiser already omits alpha: serializeStop(parseColorIn("rgb(1 2 3 / 1)","oklch")) -> "oklch(8.230913764844% 0.008035214733 240.750922799419deg)" (no `/ 1`). At alpha 0.5 it emits `/ 50%`, which the regex is anchored on the literal `1` and could not match either.
defects.mechanism: A defensive normalisation written against a serialiser behaviour that does not exist — a masking fallback for an impossible input (owner edict 2: no shims, no masking fallbacks). It is also inert against the behaviour it purports to guard, since the modern serialiser emits percentages.
defects.reproduction: node /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PreviewRamp/probe-C-edge.mjs, fields `slash1Hits` and `serializeStopAlpha1`.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the `.replace(...)`. If a canonical stamp dialect is wanted, do it deliberately and once in `stampStops` (which C-2's cure needs anyway), not by string surgery in the serialiser.

defects.defect: The entire chip is a single CSS declaration, so one unpaintable stop invalidates the whole gradient: the chip becomes a transparent hole while `data-stops` keeps claiming all 17 stops. PreviewStrip cannot fail this way (per-segment background-color costs one segment).
defects.evidence: probe-C-edge.mjs, stop 8 of 17 replaced with an unparseable colour: {"goodBg":"linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.62 0.27 9.8), ...","poisonedBg":"none","poisonedBgColor":"rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)"}. PreviewRamp.vue:35 sets the whole ramp as one `backgroundImage`; :34 computes `data-stops` independently, so the stamp survives the paint's death.
defects.mechanism: CSS gradient parsing is all-or-nothing, and the component has no background-color fallback. The O-14 law reads "the painted gradient must embed exactly those stops"; in this state it embeds none of them, and only the stamp would be checked by anything downstream.
defects.reproduction: node .../probe-C-edge.mjs, field `render.poisonedBg`. LIVE TRIGGER: NONE FOUND — labelled a robustness finding, not a live bug. I drove the boundary operands through the real sampler in-browser: `transparent` -> valid oklch(... / 0%) stops; `oklch(0.5 0.1 none)` -> the none hue collapses to a number, no `none` reaches the paint; `currentColor` -> null; "" -> null; identical operands -> 17 identical valid stops; kelvin space -> valid. Every reachable path serialises paintable OKLCh.
defects.proposedCure: C-3's hard-stop cure does not fix this (still one declaration). The structural cure is the rooted plate painting per-segment children, which makes the failure local and visible — the same move C-3 and C-6 want.

defects.defect: `sampleInterpolationRamp`'s exported `k` parameter has no domain guard and breaks the module's own contract at the boundary: k=NaN returns `[]` (neither null nor a ramp, and `[]` is truthy so the host's `v-if` does not catch it), and k=Infinity never terminates.
defects.evidence: sample.ts:52-57 documents `string[] | null`; :69 computes `perSegment = Math.max(2, Math.ceil(k / segments) + 1)`. probe-C-edge.mjs: k=0 -> 2 stops, k=1 -> 2, k=-5 -> 2 (the Math.max floor holds); k=NaN -> {"n": 0}; k=Infinity -> non-terminating (observed: hung the page for >170s, the first probe run had to be killed at the 180s tool timeout). Host guard that would miss `[]`: MixConfigBar.vue:111 `v-if="spaceRamps.get(s.value)"`.
defects.mechanism: A public exported parameter with no domain guard, in a module whose stated thesis is "honest absence, never a canned swatch". The honesty is enforced for operands (sample.ts:58 and :64) and not for k. `Math.ceil(Infinity/1)+1 = Infinity` makes the inner `for (j < perSegment)` loop non-terminating.
defects.reproduction: Direct call only. `k` is never passed by any host (MixConfigBar.vue:62 and :71 use the default 16), so neither arm is reachable from the running app today — labelled a hypothesis-grade robustness finding on that basis. To reproduce: node .../probe-C-edge.mjs (kNaN); the kInfinity arm is deliberately stubbed out in the banked probe because re-running it hangs the page.
defects.proposedCure: `if (!Number.isInteger(k) || k < 2) return null;` at the top of the function, beside the existing operand guard. One line, same idiom as the line above it.

defects.defect: `stampStops(stops)` is an unmemoised plain function call in the template, so a join over 17 long strings re-runs on every render rather than every stop change; and the host resolves each ramp twice per row (once in `v-if`, once in `:stops`).
defects.evidence: PreviewRamp.vue:34 `:data-stops="stampStops(stops)"` versus PreviewRamp.vue:24-26 where `gradient` is correctly a `computed` — the correct idiom is two lines above the defect. The sibling has the identical defect at PreviewStrip.vue:44. Host: MixConfigBar.vue:111 calls `spaceRamps.get(s.value)` twice per row and :133 likewise — 26 Map lookups per render across the two menus where 13 would do.
defects.mechanism: A template call site where the file's own established pattern is a computed. Cost is genuinely small (17 joins is microseconds, and the menu is off the critical path); it is a finding because it is per-render forever and the cure is one word.
defects.reproduction: Read PreviewRamp.vue:24-36; the asymmetry between line 24 (computed) and line 34 (bare call) is the whole evidence. NONE — no timing measurement was taken, because the component never renders (C-1), so a live cost cannot be measured today.
defects.proposedCure: `const stamp = computed(() => stampStops(stops));` and bind that. In the host, `v-for` over precomputed `{ meta, ramp }` pairs so each ramp resolves once per row.

defects.defect: The ramp direction is physical (`90deg`), not logical, so the gradient always runs left-to-right regardless of writing direction — while the thing it encodes (operand order) is a reading-order fact.
defects.evidence: PreviewRamp.vue:25 `linear-gradient(90deg, ...)`. No `dir="rtl"` exists anywhere in demo/ today, so nothing is currently broken.
defects.mechanism: A physical direction written into a component that otherwise uses logical properties throughout (`inline-size`, `block-size` at :43-44) — an inconsistency in the file's own vocabulary.
defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis. The demo has no RTL locale, so the divergence is currently unobservable.
defects.proposedCure: `to inline-end` instead of `90deg`, matching the logical-property vocabulary the rest of the block already uses.
